title: Utkal identity: warmth, knowledge and living art
description: Proposed name, visual identity, cultural reference discipline and artist collaboration direction.
body:
# Utkal identity: warmth, knowledge and living art

## User direction

The user wants investment in a name, logo, colour scheme and warm artistic assets that give the website a local and traditional flavour. This record preserves the resulting creative proposal; the name Utkal is now confirmed by the user; the earlier visual proposal is not thereby approved.

## Proposed identity

**Utkal — A living encyclopedia of Odisha.** Keep Odisha in the descriptor, discovery copy and page titles. The proposed logo integrates an open book and a boat, connecting knowledge and discovery with the project's maritime editorial theme. The mark is contemporary, not a historical emblem.

Palette: deep red `#8F2435`, warm ivory `#F5EBDD`, charcoal `#24211F`, ochre `#C9923E` and lagoon teal `#245C59`. This is art direction; no single historically definitive Odisha colour is established. Use dark readable text on quiet ivory surfaces, with illustration around story openings rather than behind statistics or paragraphs.

## Cultural references and boundaries

Reuse the saved records on [Raghurajpur and Pattachitra](../culture/raghurajpur-pattachitra.md), [Pipili appliqué](../culture/pipili-applique.md), [Sambalpuri Bandha](../handlooms/sambalpuri-bandha.md) and [Boita Bandana](../culture/boita-bandana.md) when preparing specific briefs. This reuse is not fresh independent verification. These traditions should retain their own names, contexts and practitioner credits.

The first images are AI-generated contemporary concepts using the built-in image generator, not artisan-made works, verified depictions of destinations or historical reconstructions. No named human has reviewed them. Avoid claiming that generated cloth, architecture or ornament represents an authenticated traditional design.

## Review and investment priorities

The creative recommendation is Utkal with the Odisha descriptor. The name Utkal is confirmed by the user; name/domain availability, production typography and a resolved vector identity remain open. The raster mark is a concept. A paid collaboration with Odisha artists should bring specific subjects, original artwork and visible artist credit into the finished site. Obtain a bounded quote; no budget, commission or outreach is recorded here.

The workspace deliverables are in `outputs/brand/v1/`: identity board, logo concept, coastal illustration, botanical divider, exact colour tokens, prompt/provenance record and an artist brief. They are included in the project package, not the self-contained knowledge-only bundle. The public site has not been built or published.

See [editorial direction](editorial-direction.md) and [publication readiness](website-readiness.md).

## Naming correction · 1 October 2026

Use **Utkal** in project prose and new assets. The original brand/v1 artwork and generation prompts are historical concepts with the superseded spelling, not current production assets. Exact third-party titles such as Utkala Sanskara retain their published spelling.

body:
# Utkal · Odisha — a community encyclopedia

The [detailed product requirements](../product/prd.md) now record audiences, scope, acceptance and growth programmes. Its [preserved versions](../product/versions/index.md) retain historical baselines; the initial PRD is a draft, not a claim of formal approval or implementation.

## Mission

Build a public, community-contributed encyclopedia of Odisha’s places, food, people, skills, history and development. Make its strengths vivid and useful enough that visitors, residents, journalists and government researchers return to it and cite it. Adoption is an ambition, not an achieved endorsement.

The working identity remains **Utkal · Odisha**. GitHub owner: **ahimanikya**, supplied by the user. Suggested repository name: `odisha-encyclopedia`; it has not been created or reserved remotely. The current workspace preserves the existing OKF 0.2 concept paths.

## Three connected experiences

**Discover Odisha.** Browse [nine subject families](../subjects/index.md), from people and history to health, schooling, livelihoods and the environment. Read contextual entries, data explainers, maps and cultural stories, with tourism among the featured collections. Each page explains its subject and offers relevant next reading.

**Understand and cite.** A source panel, definitions, period and geography, estimate status, calculation notes, revision history and downloadable records. A citation identifies the page, stable concept ID, version, source and relevant access date. Original sources remain prominent so researchers can inspect them.

**Contribute.** Git users submit reviewed pull requests; GitHub issue forms remain an optional account-based route.[^github-forms] The agreed launch also includes guest text contributions through Firebase Spark and photos sent to the editorial inbox, optionally through a tested free form relay. Editors publish accepted contributions through Git. These routes are planned, not yet deployed. See the [current technical stack](../technology/technical-stack.md) and [architecture diagrams](../technology/architecture.md).

## The editorial promise

Select stories that reveal Odisha’s strengths. Let independent evidence determine the facts. Preserve important comparison bases, uncertainty and corrections. Commercial relationships and funding must be disclosed. Government information is attributed to its issuing body; the encyclopedia does not imply government endorsement.

Positive coverage and rigorous correction support the same goal: a reputation readers can rely on. A genuine correction is welcome even when it makes a headline less flattering. Clearly label local testimony, folklore, interpretation, announcements and measured outcomes.

## One knowledge source, several public forms

Keep sourced knowledge in the existing Markdown and structured-data records. Public pages, charts, search and download views should be generated from those records and their approved presentation content. Avoid maintaining separate copies of the same statistic across posters and pages.

Preserve concept-path identity, such as `food/chhena-jhili`. Proposed public routes can follow these IDs once the domain and framework are chosen. Renames require aliases and redirects. A record update should reveal the dependent stories and visuals that need attention.

Publication status is separate from OKF lifecycle status and source-check metadata. A stable research method or a machine-checked source extract is not automatically a publication-approved feature. Build the public website from an explicit approved set; keep research leads and unresolved records out of visitor recommendations until suitable for that use.

## Contribution and release flow

**Propose → supply evidence → automated checks → editorial review → merge → approved release → website.**

Automated checks validate structure, references and calculations. Editors assess source quality, meaning, attribution and publication suitability. Named subject reviewers assess specialist claims when needed. GitHub branch rules can require reviews and successful checks before merge; those controls still need remote configuration.[^github-review-rules]

The local scaffold supplies contribution guidance, issue forms, a pull-request template, code ownership and a checks-only workflow. It does not deploy. Contributor checks use read-only permissions and no publishing credentials. Privileged workflows must not run untrusted contribution code.[^github-workflow-security]

## What makes an entry citable

- Stable concept ID and permanent public URL.
- A concise claim linked to the source passage, table or page where possible.
- Clear geography, dates, units, definitions and comparison basis.
- Separate source-check date, editorial-review date and publication date.
- Named contributor and reviewer only when that work actually happened.
- Revision-specific citation and downloadable data for numeric claims.
- Visible corrections, superseded versions and conflicts of interest.

A copied government number is still attributed government data. A local account is labelled testimony until independently corroborated. Our derived figures retain the inputs and calculation. AI assistance is disclosed in provenance and never substitutes for a human review badge.

## Start with complete entries across subjects

The 30 September 2026 direction broadens the encyclopedia beyond a tourism entrance. Expand the existing pages with facts, context, subject classification and explained links. Keep a single canonical record reusable across collections, and separate subject, format, geography, period and evidence state.

The [PRD](../product/prd.md) retains the Painted Streets pilot and adds proposed non-tourism reading cases for health/education and the economy. Tourism, food and heritage entries can progress alongside those subjects. Complete source and citation views and contribution guidance from the beginning; the number of pages alone is not a launch criterion.

The [classification method](../methods/content-classification.md), [visitor roadmap](../visitor-index/expansion-roadmap.md) and [statistics standard](statistics-storytelling.md) support different reading needs. Broader coverage does not imply complete district or community representation.

## Adoption and governance

Track useful contributions, correction turnaround, current source checks and external citations. Count journalistic or government references only when a saved public link demonstrates them. Do not treat a social share, page view or government source citation as an institutional endorsement.

The owner appoints topic editors and publishes funding and editorial-responsibility information. Contributors should be credited with their consent. Representation across districts and languages requires deliberate recruitment later; no outreach is authorised by this document.

## Before opening publicly

The [decision register](../technology/decisions.md) records the agreed Astro, GitHub Pages and Firebase Spark design, with AI and paid private backups deferred. Finalise the repository name and visibility, domain, content/code licences and named editorial maintainers. Confirm rights for contributed writing, images and datasets. Configure branch protection and release review. Build the website and publication selection mechanism, then review a coherent pilot collection. The local repository has no remote and the website has not been built or published.

[^github-forms]: [GitHub issue and pull request templates](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/about-issue-and-pull-request-templates)
[^github-review-rules]: [GitHub protected branches](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches)
[^github-workflow-security]: [GitHub Actions secure use](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use)

## Repository integration · 1 October 2026

This imported research describes the source workspace at its recorded dates. Utkal Project already has a repository and a published preview; current authority, implementation and release status are held in [project records](../../records/index.md) and [the operating dashboard](../../registers/DASHBOARD.md). This sync adds research for review; it does not deploy these additions or replace implemented website addenda. The scheduled research queue continues in its existing workspace pending a separate canonical-workflow handover.

body:
# Utkal Project: editorial and visual direction

Current voice and narration follow the [Utkal storytelling standard](../../reference/storytelling-standard.md), directed by the Founder on 29 September 2026 UTC. The earlier naming and palette proposals below are superseded by the settled **Utkal Project** name, **Rediscover Utkal. Reimagine Odisha.** tagline and [brand direction 02](../../reference/brand-direction-02.md). They remain here as proposal history.

## Current encyclopedia direction

The user’s 30 September 2026 direction is to expand, relate and classify content across Odisha. The [nine subject families](../subjects/index.md) give people, health, education, livelihoods, the economy, environment and governance their own reading paths alongside cultural and place knowledge. Pride and curiosity should grow from specific, supported details across these subjects.

The [tourism campaign proposal](tourism-first-strategy.md) remains one focused collection. It does not govern all research or website navigation. The user’s future personal business is not the organising premise.

## Brand proposition

**Utkal — A living encyclopedia of Odisha**

**A world of stories, waiting to be shared.**

The name and descriptor are the current [identity proposal](brand-identity.md). The second line is optional campaign copy, not a second brand name.

Use Utkal as the user’s chosen cultural expression and Odisha as the clear contemporary geographic name. Keep Odisha in page titles and search descriptions so audiences can find the work. This is a naming strategy, not a claim that historical territorial boundaries were identical in every period.

## Voice

Warm, specific and visually led. Name the food, the textile, the place and the person. Invite curiosity. Build pride through detail. Let the photograph and a short memorable line open the story; put evidence behind the detail.

Suggested recurring invitations: “Taste Odisha.” “Meet its makers.” “Follow a different road.” “See what is growing.” These are creative proposals, not existing official slogans.

## Palette proposal

| Colour | Hex | Editorial use |
|---|---|---|
| Deep red | #8F2435 | Identity and main accents |
| Warm ivory | #F5EBDD | Background and breathing room |
| Charcoal | #24211F | Text and quiet contrast |
| Ochre | #C9923E | Small highlights and chart accents |
| Lagoon teal | #245C59 | Links, secondary actions and selected data series |

This is an art-direction choice for this project. The KB has not established a single official or historically definitive colour representing all Odisha. Keep photographs true to the individual textile, food or place; do not recolour cultural objects to fit the palette.

## India and international framing

For Indian audiences, test weekend discovery, regional food and meaningful purchases as entry points. For global audiences, test making processes, named landscapes and explained cultural context. Avoid treating either audience as uniform: language, motivation and familiarity should guide later testing.

## Copy discipline

Use a strong supported detail instead of an unverified superlative. “More to discover” is an invitation; “never discovered” erases the people who know a place. A growth story needs a period and measure. A maker story needs a name and credit. A travel story needs current practical information before it becomes a recommendation.

## Presenting numbers

Follow the [statistics presentation standard](statistics-storytelling.md): one clear takeaway, one main number, a useful comparison and a simple visual. Explain what the measure means. Keep periods, units and material qualifications visible, with deeper evidence on demand.

## Name to use

The user confirmed **Utkal** on 1 October 2026. Use that spelling for this project and assistant-authored references. Preserve exact external titles and quotations.

body:
# Learning from Odisha Tourism

**Recommendation:** organise the encyclopedia around reusable place, subject, person and evidence records, then offer focused reading paths for people planning a visit. Odisha Tourism demonstrates how discovery can lead into practical planning; Utkal can connect that experience to a broader account of Odisha’s culture, livelihoods and development.

The initial **nine-page sample reviewed on 30 September 2026** was supplemented by the tour-guide directory and a visual icon review the same day: **ten distinct pages in total**, not a whole-site audit. It includes the homepage, road-trip listing and one detail, trail finder, map, handloom theme, Raghurajpur, wayside amenities and artisan stories. Browser inspection covered road cards, expanded trail filters, the map page and the loaded road-trip detail. The other pages were read through HTML extraction. No enquiry, booking, login, location permission or contact submission was performed.

## What they have organised well

The portal separates discovery, experience, planning, shopping and departmental information. A reader can enter through a destination, a cultural interest or a practical travel task.[^odisha-tourism-portal] This offers a useful model for multiple entrances to shared information.

| Observed pattern | What the sample establishes | What Utkal should learn |
|---|---|---|
| Trip cards | Road-trip cards expose duration, covered places, attractions and detail links.[^tourism-roadtrips] | Give readers enough context to decide which guide to open |
| Planning filters | Opening the trail filters revealed day-type and activity choices and a location/name search; provider/sort controls and loaded cards were visible.[^tourism-trail-finder] | Let visitors narrow by time, interest and place, using fields with known values |
| Itinerary detail | The sampled road trip includes a summary, audience/terrain tags, day tabs, first-day transport fields, food/shopping and emergency sections.[^tourism-wild-west-route] | Store itinerary stops and travel legs as explicit records, with their own evidence |
| Map and list | Search, categories and destination entries appear alongside map/list controls.[^tourism-map-finder] | Keep a usable list even when a map cannot load; validate coordinates before plotting |
| Rich destination page | Raghurajpur combines an introduction, stays, stories, essentials, related places and travel/weather sections.[^raghurajpur] | Build a consistent place-page template joining inspiration and practical details |
| Themes across geography | The handloom page connects textile discussion with several production centres.[^weaving-tourism] | A tradition can link to several places and collections without duplicated articles |
| Support infrastructure | The wayside page gives amenities a dedicated entrance, though the extracted inventory did not populate.[^tourism-wayside] | Toilets, rest stops, transport and accessibility deserve structured records |
| People and commerce | An artisan-story entrance and store-locator link exist; individual narratives were not readable in this capture.[^tourism-artisan-stories] | Create credited maker profiles, then verify any workshop or buying relationship |

Interface presence is different from functional verification. Opening the filter panel worked; complete filtering, geolocation, itinerary calculation and booking flows were not tested. The visible trail count is a website claim, not an independently audited inventory, so it has not been added to our statistical atlas.

## The organisation to adopt

Keep the existing nine subjects as the encyclopedia’s foundation. Retain the PRD’s broad entrances—subjects, places, numbers, stories and contribution—and offer **Visit Odisha**, **Made in Odisha** and **Life in Odisha** as focused collections. A reader researching education should reach education directly.

Within Visit Odisha, offer four reading paths:

1. **Choose a place:** destination areas, districts and cities, with their distinct geographic scope visible.
2. **Choose an interest:** food, craft, heritage, nature, performance and city experiences.
3. **Prepare a visit:** access, transport, stays, food providers, facilities and official assistance.
4. **Explore a journey:** reviewed itineraries once route and operating evidence is complete; until then, clearly labelled research outlines.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[Subject or interest] --> P[Canonical place record]
  R[Regional guide] --> P
  P --> C[Culture, food and makers]
  P --> F[Visitor services]
  P --> E[Dated facts and sources]
  P --> J[Itinerary stop]
  J --> L[Verified travel leg]
```

The diagram is a proposed content model, not a deployed interface. Geography, topic, content type, season, visit duration, audience needs and evidence status are separate dimensions. Unknown duration or accessibility must remain unknown; “family friendly” needs stated supporting features, not a decorative label.

## A place page readers can use

Start with a concise introduction and credited image, followed by “Why it matters”, “Explore”, “Food and makers”, “Plan a visit”, “Related places” and “Sources and corrections”. Keep the main story readable and reveal detailed evidence on demand.

In the planning panel, use field-level dates: access rules, opening hours, fees, transport, toilets, drinking water, step-free access and official contact. Describe verified features rather than issuing a blanket accessibility or safety score. Separate accommodation elsewhere in a region from accommodation with measured proximity to the place.

**Worked example: Raghurajpur.** Connect our [craft record](../culture/raghurajpur-pattachitra.md) to the [Puri craft-area guide](../visitor-index/areas/puri-crafts.md), [Made in Odisha](../collections/made-in-odisha.md) and evidence about the tradition. Leave named willing hosts, current workshop hours, food-serving venues and point-to-point journeys as explicit research gaps. Do not assign a duration or a “nearby” radius from the editorial grouping.

## What to improve when adapting the model

The Raghurajpur page’s nearby introduction names Sukuapada, and its accommodation section includes several other destinations. That is a concrete reason to check context and location before importing relationships; those listings do not establish local proximity.[^raghurajpur]

The sampled road detail has differing summary/description route labels and an old event window. Its transport and emergency fields need fresh checks before reuse.[^tourism-wild-west-route] Preserve the useful structure, while independently validating the contents.

Use separate labels for official editorial material, operator offers, contributor stories and measured statistics. Views, promotional rankings and reviews do not establish visits, service quality or economic impact. Do not interpret text-extraction gaps as proof that a service is absent. Retain spelling aliases while resolving identity; similar labels are not enough to merge records.

## Tour planning in practical stages

| Stage | Recommended work | Release condition |
|---|---|---|
| Apply now to the KB | Organise existing entries by place, interest and planning need; use the new trip-research template | Preserve IDs, source dates, qualifiers and explained links |
| First usable visitor guides | Deepen one area into a complete guide, with a printable reading version and official onward links | Named review plus current access, route and facility evidence |
| Later product proposal | Filter reviewed guides by start place, available time, interests and substantiated access needs; save a shortlist and offer map/list views | Explicit scope decision, populated data and tested interaction |
| Separate future decision | Automatic route optimisation, live availability, booking or operator enquiry transmission | Reliable data/services, defined operating responsibility and revised requirements |

**Start with Puri and the craft corridor**, where linked food, heritage and facility records already exist. Then deepen Koraput and Sambalpur–Bargarh for regional breadth. These are research priorities, not currently validated travel itineraries.

## Connected planning and a consistent icon vocabulary

The user highlighted the portal’s hierarchy, planning, tour guides and icon system as useful references. The suggested resemblance to TripAdvisor is an **unverified design hypothesis**; this study does not establish the portal’s design lineage.

The practical pattern to adapt is **discover a place → explore experiences → read a journey → find people and services → check current details**. These are connected entry points, not a requirement that every reader follow a fixed sequence. Keep them within Visit Odisha while maintaining direct access to the encyclopedia’s other subjects.

The [Get a Tour Guide directory](../sources/tourism-guide-directory.md) exposes district/location/city/name search, filter and sorting controls, and a contact-details section.[^tourism-guide-directory] Individual profiles and totals did not populate in the extracted text. The directory is a discovery reference; no guide’s credentials, availability or quality has been verified. Keep a **written travel guide**, a **person working as a tour guide** and a **travel agency** as distinct record types. Link professional profiles to places served, languages, specialisms and sourced credentials; a “most liked” sort is not a quality assessment.

A supplementary browser screenshot of the road-trip summary shows thin outline pictograms grouped by traveller type and terrain, with section tabs and a map below.[^tourism-wild-west-route] This is useful visual shorthand. In the captured narrow view, the small individual pictograms do not have visible text labels; Utkal should pair them with short labels, especially for unfamiliar meanings.

| Proposed icon family | Example meanings | Presentation rule |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery | Place, food, handloom, heritage, nature | Icon plus familiar subject name |
| Planning | Duration, route, transport, stay, tour guide, facilities | Pair with a sourced value or explicit unknown state |
| Wider encyclopedia | Health, education, industry, trade, data | Share the same visual family across subjects |
| Interface actions | Search, filter, map/list, save, sources | Accessible names; visible selected/focus states; never colour alone |

Start with original or clearly licensed SVG icons on a consistent 24-pixel grid and stroke system, checked at actual display sizes. These dimensions are a proposal, not measurements of Odisha Tourism’s assets. Use the existing charcoal/teal/red palette on ivory with tested contrast; reserve local art for credited illustrations and selective accents. The source icon package and licence are unknown, and no source assets were copied. The [brand notes](../../reference/brand-direction-02.md) carry the proposed direction. No icon library or planner has been implemented by this study.

## Product traceability and maintenance

The recommendations elaborate existing DISC-001/004/005 (navigation, connections and classification) and CONT-001/002/003/006 (page structure, evidence, credit and freshness). The [current PRD](../product/prd.md) remains v0.2.0. Planner interactions and transactional services above are proposals; none is silently added to launch scope or marked implemented. Promote an adopted material feature through the existing PRD version process.

- [Trip-planning content template](../methods/trip-planning-content.md) — Turn a journey idea into a record with explicit evidence gaps.
- [Visitor collection](../visitor-index/index.md) — Browse the reorganised local entry points.
- [Saved observations and mapping](../references/data/tourism-reference-study.json) — Review source scopes and the adaptation decisions.


[^odisha-tourism-portal]: [Odisha Tourism — official visitor portal](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en.html).

[^tourism-roadtrips]: [Odisha By Road](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/plan/trip-organizer/find-a-roadtrip.html).

[^tourism-trail-finder]: [Find a Trail](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/plan/trip-organizer/find-trail.html).

[^tourism-map-finder]: [Find on Map](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/plan/trip-organizer/find-on-map.html).

[^tourism-wayside]: [Way Side Amenities](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/plan/food-accommodation/way-side-ammenities.html).

[^tourism-artisan-stories]: [Artisan Stories](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/shopping/brickMortarStores/shopArtisanStories.html).

[^tourism-wild-west-route]: [The Quest for Odishas Wild West — road-trip detail](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/road-trip-detail/the-quest-for-odishas-wild-west.html).

[^raghurajpur]: [Raghurajpur](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/discover/attractions/arts-crafts/raghurajpur.html).

[^weaving-tourism]: [Handloom](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/experience/themes/handloom.html).

[^tourism-guide-directory]: [Get a Tour Guide](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/plan/trip-organizer/tour-guide.html).

title: What the first research edition reveals

body:
# What the first research edition reveals

The strongest opportunity is to make Odisha specific. A name, a place, a process and a person give a reader something to remember and a reason to explore further. This is an editorial inference from the collected material, not a measured conclusion about public awareness.

## 1. Food can become a destination in its own right

The collection already separates breakfast and everyday dishes, pitha, dairy sweets, leaf cooking and place-linked ingredients. [Pitha](../food/pitha.md) provides a multi-part series rather than one generic food post. [Chhena poda](../food/chhena-poda.md) offers a visually accessible introduction; [Koraput coffee](../food/koraput-coffee.md) and [Kalajeera rice](../food/koraput-kalajeera-rice.md) let the story begin with producers.

For Indian audiences, test familiar entry points such as breakfast, festivals and regional food journeys. For international audiences, explain ingredient and technique in plain language while retaining the Odia name. These are audience hypotheses to test. The evidence does not yet quantify culinary variety, market penetration or awareness.

## 2. Textiles need individual identities

[Kotpad](../handlooms/kotpad.md), [Khandua](../handlooms/khandua.md), [Habaspuri](../handlooms/habaspuri.md) and [Berhampuri Patta](../handlooms/berhampuri-patta.md) deserve separate stories. “Odisha handloom” is the collection name, not a substitute for provenance. A useful product page would show fibre, technique, making place, maker and object-specific care.

The commercial opportunity to investigate is a path from appreciation to a credited maker or traceable seller. No sales-growth or under-marketing estimate has been established. Existing promotion, including tourism material and [Boyanika](../handlooms/boyanika.md), means “never marketed” would be inaccurate.

## 3. Tourism becomes richer when places connect

A monument page is useful; a [coast-and-culture story](../stories/coast-and-culture.md) gives it context. A landscape can lead to a textile and then an ingredient in [Koraput](../stories/koraput.md). [Western Odisha](../stories/western-odisha.md) deserves an editorial chapter of its own. These proposed journeys are content structures; travel time, hosts, seasonality and booking details still need work.

## 4. Recognition should be precise

[Konark](../places/konark.md), [Chilika](../places/chilika.md), [Similipal](../places/similipal.md) and [Mayurbhanj Chhau](../culture/mayurbhanj-chhau.md) connect to different international programmes. Give each its actual recognition, date and scope. Combining them under an invented universal UNESCO badge would weaken the work.

## 5. Growth adds a contemporary chapter

The [economic collection](../economy/index.md) adds industry, fisheries and logistics to the cultural picture. It also retains tourism’s recovery alongside its longer comparison. An attractive campaign can select strong, supported stories while preserving enough context to make the numbers understandable.

## What makes the next edition deeper

The next gains come from local voices, specialist review and original media: a cook demonstrating a variant; a weaver explaining a piece; a guide explaining a landscape; a resident showing a neighbourhood. Those details will turn this research foundation into distinctive features.

title: Research gaps and source conflicts
description: Research gaps and source conflicts — research and reuse notes.
body:
# Research gaps and source conflicts

## Priority research queue

| Priority | Work | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Food depth | Attributed recipes and variations for six pitha, four everyday dishes and four place-linked sweets; Odia script and pronunciation reviewed by a fluent editor |
| 1 | Textile depth | Maker-reviewed fibre, technique, motif and care notes for six traditions; consented portraits and documented seller provenance |
| 1 | Tourism usability | Five journeys with realistic travel times, seasonal access, willing hosts, practical services and clear source dates |
| 1 | Economic refresh | Latest survey and revisions; comparable historical GSDP endpoints and source locations; retain complete series |
| 2 | District breadth | Coverage map across all 30 districts, with priority for currently missing southern, western and interior places |
| 2 | City life | Representative resident interviews, transport and neighbourhood data, current venues and comparable cost indicators |
| 2 | Market evidence | Search-interest baselines, destination awareness interviews, textile distribution and sales evidence; define “under-marketed” before measuring it |
| 2 | Crafts and ingredients | Cuttack Tarakasi; additional craft forms; millets, greens, fish preparations and community-specific food traditions using specialist/local sources |
| 3 | Language editions | Odia and Hindi editorial review; internationally understandable descriptions; no automatic transliteration presented as verified |

## Conflict: Deomali elevation

The [destination profile](../places/deomali.md) gives 1,762 m, while the [district overview source](../sources/koraput.md) gives 1,672 m. title: How knowledge is recorded and reused
description: How knowledge is recorded and reused — research and reuse notes.
body:
# How knowledge is recorded and reused

## What this collection contains

This bundle follows the published Open Knowledge Format 0.2: concept documents in Markdown with YAML metadata, source references, lifecycle fields and linked indexes.[^okf] The producer’s additional fields describe geography, aliases, evidence status and publication readiness. They are local extensions, not new OKF requirements.

## Three layers

1. **Sourced knowledge:** a narrow factual statement tied to a source, with the source’s scope retained.
2. **Interpretation and creative proposals:** editorial choices, campaign language and suggested connections. These are not measured findings.
3. **Open research:** missing local detail, disagreements, operational checks and questions requiring specialist or participant input.

## Evidence handling

Primary registries support designation claims. Statistical publications support named measures and periods. Institutional tourism pages support destination and cultural descriptions, but promotional assertions still require judgment. A contributor post on a government-hosted site remains a contributor post; a chef interview describes that chef’s account, not every household’s practice.

New cultural records were checked against targeted web page or PDF extracts. Their verification scope is stated in metadata. Some source access consisted of indexed passages, not complete PDFs. Source entries disclose this; the collection does not pretend to contain complete archived originals. Only concise extracted knowledge and bibliographic information are retained.

Earlier economic and city evidence was migrated with its original caveats. It is marked as imported and has no new source-verification event. Recalculating a percentage establishes arithmetic consistency, not source accuracy. No record claims human review.

## Freshness

Review dates are editorial schedules. They do not mean a historical designation expires on that date. Recheck financial releases after the next survey; live travel information before each publication; registry validity before a current GI claim; and historical/cultural records annually or when new evidence appears.

## Reuse

Search locally first. Follow the source and caveat for a proposed claim. If the record answers a stable historical question, reuse the saved nucleus. Browse again when the question is new, the record is stale, sources conflict or a current operational detail is needed. Add the result here so the same research is not repeated.

This edition is a substantial starting collection. It is not a census of Odisha’s foods, communities, textiles or destinations.

[^okf]: [Open Knowledge Format, version 0.2](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md)

title: Making Odisha’s numbers easy to understand
description: A story-led presentation standard for statistics, visitor indexes, posters and videos.
evidence_status: Editorial guidance; numerical examples reuse existing KB records without new source verification.
body:
# Making Odisha’s numbers easy to understand

The user wants statistics to be consumable, meaningful and easy to read. Lead with a memorable takeaway, a clearly labelled number and its relevance to the reader. Keep the research depth available behind the experience.

## The public unit: one small story

1. **Headline:** say what changed or why the detail is interesting.
2. **Hero number:** one main statistic, with its measure and period alongside it.
3. **Meaning:** one sentence explaining what it tells us. Connect it to a person, place or experience only where evidence supports that connection.
4. **Visual:** use the simplest form that makes the point clear: a labelled comparison, a short trend, a map or a credited photograph.
5. **Invitation and evidence:** offer a relevant next step and an expandable source/method panel. Keep any qualification that changes the headline’s meaning visible beside the number.

Aim for a takeaway in three seconds, understanding in thirty seconds, and deeper evidence on demand. These are design targets, not measured audience results. Test actual comprehension with readers later.

## Make the format fit the subject

- **Growth:** one headline and a small chart showing the full relevant period. Label the start and end; show intervening years when available.
- **Food:** a named dish, an appetising credited photograph, its place association and a short reason to try it. Add a serving venue once established.
- **Heritage:** a distinctive detail, a strong image and a clear location. Add visitor information where checked.
- **Facilities:** readable service labels with location and freshness information. Distinguish “listed by the operator” from currently confirmed availability.
- **Regional collections:** a map or a few destination cards with filters. A research entry count is a count of this collection, not Odisha’s total food or heritage inventory.

Default to one main number per card, one story per poster and one main idea per short video. On an opening screen, use at most three supporting facts before inviting the reader to explore. These are project defaults; clarity takes precedence over a rigid count.

## Draft examples from the saved research

These examples demonstrate presentation. They reuse imported source data and checked arithmetic; they have not received a fresh source check or publication review in this update.

### Tourism: a recovery story

**Tourist visits rose 13.1% in 2024**

**1.11 crore visits** · Odisha · calendar year 2024

Up from 97.7 lakh in 2023—about 12.8 lakh additional recorded visits in a year.

**Visible context:** This is a one-year recovery comparison. Visits remained below the 2019 level of 1.54 crore. Counts cover domestic and foreign tourist visits, not unique people.

**Visual direction:** show 2019, 2023 and 2024 as three labelled bars starting at zero. Identify them as selected years; do not draw a continuous annual trend through missing years.

**Next action:** Explore Odisha’s destinations.

**Evidence:** [2023–2024 comparison](../economy/comparison-10-tourism.md) and [2019 benchmark](../economy/comparison-09-tourism.md). For an international edition, display 11.1 million visits instead of 1.11 crore. Exact values remain in the linked records.

### Manufacturing: growth with its basis explained

**Manufacturing’s economic contribution grew 26% over five years**

**26% real growth** · Odisha · FY2019–20 to FY2024–25

The sector added more economic value after adjusting for price changes. This measure does not establish growth in jobs, company sales or investment.

**Visible caption:** Manufacturing gross state value added at constant 2011–12 prices. FY2024–25 is a first revised estimate. Rounded from 26.2%.

**Visual direction:** show all six saved annual observations so the rise, subsequent fall and recovery remain visible. Avoid an arrow implying uninterrupted annual growth.

**Next action:** Explore the manufacturing story.

**Evidence:** [Saved manufacturing series and source](../economy/manufacturing.md).

## Readable numbers and honest visuals

Use lakh and crore for Indian audiences; use million and billion for international audiences. Keep the currency visible and avoid currency conversion unless its date and exchange-rate basis are saved. Round deliberately: one decimal place is usually enough for percentages. Calculate changes from the underlying values before rounding.

Keep calendar years separate from financial years; real growth separate from nominal growth; percentage change separate from percentage-point change; visitors separate from visits; announcements separate from realised outcomes. Rankings need the ranked group, measure and year beside them.

Use direct labels, readable text and strong contrast. Avoid 3D charts, decorative gauges, crowded legends and colour-only meanings. Bar charts begin at zero. Explain a restricted line-chart scale when used. Do not hide a material benchmark or estimate status in a source drawer.

Sources, exact values, calculation notes and fuller tables belong in the evidence view, with downloadable data available for readers who want it. Public pages should answer a reader’s question before presenting additional detail.

## Keep curiosity connected to action

A tourism statistic can introduce an exploration page. A food story can lead to a confirmed maker or venue. A textile story can lead to a credited artisan and purchase route. A production statistic can lead to a sourced industry profile. Do not infer job creation, tourist spending or local income from a different measure.

Measure whether readers understand and remember the takeaway, then whether they save, share, explore or enquire. Positive audience response is a research question until observed.

# Tourism first: build attention, pride and demand for Odisha

**Scope update — 30 September 2026.** The user has clarified that the encyclopedia must expand and connect subjects beyond tourism. The [nine subject families](../subjects/index.md) now organise the overall collection. This page preserves the tourism campaign proposal from 27 September; its sequencing applies to that campaign, not to the encyclopedia’s full research or launch scope.

## Purpose and order

Build a compelling public reputation for Odisha that motivates people within the state and draws interest from India and the wider world. Tourism is the first practical focus. Food, handlooms, culture, landscape and city experiences supply the opening stories. Better trade and business opportunities are the longer-term objective.

The user’s eventual personal venture does not determine the campaign. Health and fitness, mineral processing and other industries are possible later chapters. A podcast is a possible later format, not a production commitment or a prerequisite for starting.

This campaign direction records the user’s instruction of 27 September 2026. The broader encyclopedia scope was clarified on 30 September: economic, historical, environmental and human-development knowledge have their own value and entrances.

## What the audience should take away

| Audience | Intended response | Useful next action |
|---|---|---|
| People in Odisha, including the diaspora | Pride, possibility and recognition of specific local strengths | Share a story, contribute knowledge, nominate a maker or host |
| People elsewhere in India | Curiosity and a concrete reason to explore Odisha | Save a journey, read a food feature, enquire about a visit |
| International audiences | A clear, memorable introduction to places and people | Explore an explained itinerary, meet a maker, seek a relevant connection |

These are campaign objectives. Audience response and business impact have not yet been measured.

## Editorial promise

**Utkal · Odisha — more to discover, more to share.**

Make Odisha desirable through specific experiences. Let readers see what they could taste, learn, wear, explore or participate in. Use economic achievements when they reinforce confidence in contemporary Odisha. The maritime identity can give a feature depth without requiring every tourism story to become a trade-history lesson.

## First pilot: six stories, two formats each

Develop a short video treatment and a saveable poster or carousel for each selected story. This proposed twelve-piece pilot is a manageable learning batch, not a scheduled publishing commitment. Selection depends on available media, verified details and willing contributors.

| Creative opening | Research anchor | What the feature must deliver |
|---|---|---|
| Your next journey could begin with a dish | [Pitha collection](../food/pitha.md) | Distinct named preparations, credited cook and verified recipe context |
| Follow the coast. Stay for the stories. | [Coast and culture](../stories/coast-and-culture.md) | A coherent invitation connecting place, food and making; logistics before itinerary claims |
| Meet the hands behind the cloth | [Woven Odisha](../stories/woven-odisha.md) | A named maker, a specific textile and a traceable next step |
| A landscape you can taste | [Koraput](../stories/koraput.md) | Locally grounded links among landscape, ingredients and makers |
| Follow the thread west | [Western Odisha](../stories/western-odisha.md) | A distinct regional perspective with local contributors |
| Meet the city with someone who calls it home | [Bhubaneswar](../cities/bhubaneswar.md) and [Cuttack](../cities/cuttack.md) | A resident-led experience with current, checked visitor details |

All opening lines above are creative proposals. They are not rankings, counts of all available experiences or claims of measured audience demand.

## A shareable data point needs a story

For each candidate, save four things: the exact supported claim, its source and date, the visual that explains it, and why someone would pass it on. A recognition, a specific technique or a surprising place connection can be as useful as a large number.

Use this compact content structure:

1. **Opening:** one memorable idea that is understandable without prior knowledge of Odisha.
2. **Proof:** a sourced detail, dated number, documented process or attributed voice.
3. **Experience:** show what the reader could see, taste, learn or do.
4. **Invitation:** one relevant next step, such as saving, sharing, discovering a maker or planning a visit.

Do not force an impressive-looking number into every piece. Counts of dishes in our selection are not counts of Odisha’s entire cuisine. An old city ranking is not a current universal liveability verdict. Keep essential qualifications in the visible caption.

## How to learn what spreads

Treat virality as a result to observe. Test alternative openings while keeping the underlying claim fixed. Compare similar formats and reporting windows, and record whether reach was organic or paid.

Track three layers separately: attention (reach, completion and shares per reach); interest (saves, meaningful replies and visits to fuller stories); and action (qualified tourism enquiries, maker referrals and attributable bookings or purchases). A popular post does not by itself establish increased tourism or economic impact. Establish a baseline before drawing growth conclusions.

Preserve useful audience questions and contributor suggestions in the KB, with consent where personal material is involved. Those questions can shape the next research and production batch.

## Website and podcast sequence

The tourism collection should help visitors discover and act through places, foods, textiles and stories, supported by a readable source layer. Overall website navigation follows the broader [current PRD](../product/prd.md); growth, maritime and everyday-life knowledge are independent subject content.

A podcast can grow from subjects that repeatedly attract substantive interest and guests with firsthand knowledge. Possible guest roles include a cook, weaver, guide, tourism operator, cultural researcher and founder. Each conversation should reveal a place or practice, examine an opportunity and offer a useful next step. Short extracts can feed the same story collection.

Before commissioning a season, establish the editorial theme, available guests and an achievable production rhythm. No guest outreach, recording, AI-clone production or publishing is authorised merely by this planning document.

## What happens next in the work

Prioritise the six pilot research anchors, identify the best available visual and contributor for each, and complete only the factual gaps needed for those stories. Develop health, education, livelihoods, environment and industry pages in their own right within the broader KB. Make the first public experience feel like an invitation to Odisha.

## Tourism collection priorities

The campaign’s [linked food, heritage and facilities index](../visitor-index/index.md). Deepen usable destination pages, then progressively add the other [discovery indexes](../visitor-index/expansion-roadmap.md). Specific, supported experiences should build pride and interest in Odisha.

# Website plan and publication readiness

There is enough material to define the website’s identity and build its editorial structure. A polished public launch still needs original or licensed media, local review and practical information for the journeys it recommends.

## Current technology plan

The [technology collection](../technology/index.md) records the user-agreed launch architecture and [growth roadmap](../technology/growth-roadmap.md). Use Astro/TypeScript and GitHub Pages, with Git-maintained read-only knowledge and Firebase Spark for private dynamic text. Receive photos through email or a tested free relay; publish approved copies manually through Git. AI chat, Blaze and paid private backups are deferred. These choices supersede earlier unspecified-host and account-free-intake-later proposals; implementation remains pending.

## Broad encyclopedia, connected collections

The latest user direction (30 September 2026) is to expand, relate and classify facts across Odisha. The [subject directory](../subjects/index.md) provides nine entrances spanning geography, history, people, arts, farming, environment, everyday life, economy and governance. The [classification register](../references/data/content-classification.json) assigns a primary subject and optional additional subjects to canonical records; it does not change evidence or publication status.

Tourism, food, handloom and city-experience features remain valuable collections. Health, education, livelihoods, infrastructure and public services have independent reading paths. A public entry should explain what its evidence means, show periods and caveats, and tell readers why related pages are useful. Topic association alone does not establish a causal or historical connection.

The [current PRD](../product/prd.md) retains the Painted Streets pilot and proposes non-tourism health/education and economy explainers to demonstrate breadth. Select complete, reviewed entries; a fixed page count is not the launch gate. Tourism recommendations need checked logistics, while dated statistical explanations need appropriate evidence and comparison review. A podcast and personal ventures do not determine encyclopedia coverage.

## Readiness today

| Component | State |
|---|---|
| Content architecture and editorial direction | Drafted |
| Name, palette, logo and illustration direction | First AI-generated concept kit prepared; production identity and local artist collaboration pending |
| Sourced food, textile, destination and culture nuclei | Available in this KB |
| Existing economic/city evidence and growth calculations | Preserved; calculation checks provided |
| Complete food recipes and Odia-language review | Pending |
| Maker interviews, credited portraits and verified purchase routes | Pending |
| Licensed photography and video library | Pending |
| Current travel logistics and operating information | Pending |
| User’s AI-clone service and production access | Not established in this task |

## Publishing workflow

Select a concept, complete its open research, develop the feature, confirm media rights and participant attribution, check changing facts, then record the final review. Keep the durable knowledge here even if the public copy is shorter. Each public feature should carry its KB concept IDs internally so a source update can identify affected pages.

No public website has been built or published as part of this research edition.

The user has since authorised weekly autonomous updates to the Git repository and website. The [weekly agent](../methods/weekly-data-agent.md) is active for local source monitoring and validated KB updates. Remote publication remains pending the actual GitHub connection, initial project onboarding and website deployment; this is a setup gap, not a recurring approval requirement.

## Maritime layer

Add an optional “Trade & the World” collection using the [evidence map](../history/maritime-evidence.md) and [qualified linked data](../methods/maritime-linked-data.md). Historical and contemporary layers should remain visually distinct. Each edge needs a source reveal; no diagram should imply continuous routes or causation where only an editorial pairing exists.

## Linked visitor indexes

The [visitor index](../visitor-index/index.md) now connects five areas to food, heritage and facility records. Use it for Explore, Taste and Plan your visit. Facility listings are a research seed: current operating checks, named food providers, routes and credited media remain launch requirements. The indexes are directories, not scored state rankings.

## Reader-facing statistics

Use [small, meaningful data stories](statistics-storytelling.md) throughout the website. Present visitor indexes as browsable destination, food and service cards. Keep detailed research tables in an optional evidence view. User comprehension and usefulness guide the design; large data grids are not the default public experience.

## Community encyclopedia direction

The user now wants a public, Git-backed encyclopedia with contributions through GitHub, intended owner `ahimanikya`. The [community model](community-encyclopedia.md) adds contributor review, versioned citations, corrections and explicit publication selection. The local GitHub templates and checks are prepared; the public site, remote settings and release pipeline remain to be implemented. Journalistic and government reference use is an aspiration to measure through actual citations.

## Growth-journey collection

Add four optional story entrances: [Smart cities](../journeys/smart-cities.md), [Rare earths](../journeys/rare-earths.md), [Semiconductors](../journeys/semiconductors.md) and [Investment in Odisha](../journeys/investment.md). Use one lead statistic and a dated timeline or simple chart; retain evidence-state labels. These belong within economy, infrastructure and governance, with links to relevant environmental and livelihood questions.

## Statistical atlas

A broad [source-linked atlas](../statistics/index.md) now supports concise topic stories and a district banking layer. Source conflicts and indexed-only captures are marked for further review. Research depth does not automatically make every observation ready for a public headline.


## Learning from the official tourism portal · 30 September 2026

The [reference study](../about/odisha-tourism-study.md) examines ten sampled pages and proposes place/interest/planning entrances, consistent destination modules and explicit itinerary evidence. The local visitor index now offers those reading paths. The [trip-content template](../methods/trip-planning-content.md) guides research; interactive filters, map planning, route optimisation and booking remain proposals, not additions to the launch requirements. PRD v0.2.0 and its preserved snapshots are unchanged.

## Repository integration · 1 October 2026

This imported research describes the source workspace at its recorded dates. Utkal Project already has a repository and a published preview; current authority, implementation and release status are held in [project records](../../records/index.md) and [the operating dashboard](../../registers/DASHBOARD.md). This sync adds research for review; it does not deploy these additions or replace implemented website addenda. The scheduled research queue continues in its existing workspace pending a separate canonical-workflow handover.

# Bhubaneswar: city life with cultural depth

Bhubaneswar’s initial research file combines city indicators with cultural experiences. The stored [Ease of Living rank](../evidence/u01.md) belongs to the 2020 edition and its population category. The [Swachh Survekshan result](../evidence/u04.md) belongs to the 2024–25 edition. Neither establishes a current all-purpose “best city” claim.

## Marketing opportunity

Create a resident-hosted day: breakfast, an Old Town encounter, a craft or museum visit, and an evening chosen by an actual resident. [Korakhai](../food/korakhai.md) provides one specific food connection. [The existing visitor-experience record](../evidence/u12.md) offers starting points for further research.

## Planning and infrastructure

The [BDA town-planning mechanism](../evidence/u07.md) documents land pooling and plot readjustment. [Declarations of intention](../evidence/u08.md) are planning stages, not completed infrastructure. The [Gujarat comparator](../evidence/u10.md) prevents a misleading claim of national uniqueness.

## Research still needed

Collect neighbourhood-level transport, current public spaces, representative rents, university and workplace locations, resident interviews, venue choices and measured air-quality data. The research has not established comparative nightlife quality, broad affordability, a youth-friendliness rank or consistently low pollution. Use named experiences until those comparisons exist.

body:
# Life in Odisha

What does access to learning, care, work and everyday services look like? Start with one measure at a time, keep the date in view, and follow it to the questions that matter for people’s lives. These are statewide observations, not a city liveability ranking.

## Learning: the scale of the school system

**61,565 schools** — Schools. Academic year 2024–25; Odisha.[^people-udise2025]

The administrative return covers all school management types in the reporting system. Count schools alongside learning outcomes, attendance, staffing and the reliability of facilities; institution counts alone do not measure education quality.

## Health: a broader reach of financial coverage

**47.9% → 82.7% of households** with at least one usual member covered by health insurance or a financing scheme, comparing NFHS-5 (2019–21) as reproduced in the NFHS-6 release with NFHS-6 (2023–24). Odisha’s latter fieldwork ran **18 July–28 November 2024**.[^people-nfhs6]

This is a survey comparison. It does not mean every household member was insured, that every claim was paid or that out-of-pocket costs disappeared. The [health evidence](../statistics/health.md) also retains maternal and child-service measures, including near-flat observations.

## Connection: a dated subscription count

**30.56 million subscriptions** — Internet subscriptions. 2026-03-31; Odisha.[^weekly-trai-mar2026]

Subscriptions are not unique people. This counts wired and wireless, broadband and narrowband connections; it does not measure speed, affordability or reliability. We do not compute an unqualified growth rate against the earlier release because some earlier operator data were carried forward.

## Build out the everyday picture

| Dimension | Evidence to explore | What readers still need |
|---|---|---|
| Work and participation | [Employment](../statistics/employment.md) and [women and inclusion](../statistics/women-and-inclusion.md) | Earnings, hours, job quality and rural–urban differences |
| Health and nutrition | [Health](../statistics/health.md) and [nutrition](../statistics/nutrition.md) | Service quality, affordability and outcomes across groups |
| Essential services | [Rural water](../statistics/rural-water.md) and [digital connectivity](../statistics/digital-connectivity.md) | Reliability and household experience, beyond recorded connections |
| City services | [Smart-city journey](../journeys/smart-cities.md) | Operating services, accessibility, maintenance and resident outcomes |
| Place differences | [Koraput](../places/koraput.md) and [Sambalpur–Bargarh](../places/sambalpur-bargarh.md) | Comparable district measures; statewide averages cannot fill gaps |

## A useful next contribution

Bring a dated district or city source with a defined population, unit and method. We can connect housing costs, commute times, air quality, public spaces, cultural activity and safety once comparable evidence is available. Keep adverse and flat results alongside improvements. Any future composite index needs transparent weights, coverage and missing-data rules; none is claimed here.


[^people-udise2025]: [UDISE+ 2024–25 Report: Existing Structure](https://dashboard.udiseplus.gov.in/report2025/static/media/UDISE%2B2024_25_Booklet_existing.118ba29d4773e6372f72.pdf).

[^people-nfhs6]: [National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6), 2023–2024: Fact Sheets](https://www.nfhsiips.in/nfhsuser/assets/National%20Family%20Health%20Survey%20%28NFHS-6%29%202023-2024%20Fact%20Sheets.pdf).

[^weekly-trai-mar2026]: [TRAI telecom performance indicators, January–March 2026](https://trai.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-06/QPIR_22062026.pdf).


## Connected reading

- [Odisha progress: what the evidence shows](progress.md) — Read infrastructure completion separately from service quality.
- [Education](../statistics/education.md) — Follow school counts to the underlying administrative definitions.
- [Health](../statistics/health.md) — Keep survey periods and household-coverage definitions visible.

# Made in Odisha

Discover the things Odisha grows, weaves and makes—and follow the people and places behind them. This collection joins craft, food and enterprise research. It is an editorial collection, not a certification label or a verified supplier directory.

## The people behind the cloth

**53,472 workers** — Handloom weavers. 2019–20 Handloom Census; Odisha.[^connect-handloom2019]

The same 2019–20 census records **64,364 allied workers**, a separate category. These historical counts make the scale of work visible; they do not establish today’s workforce, wages or growth.[^connect-handloom2019]

## Follow a product back to its place

| Explore | Read next | What to document with contributors |
|---|---|---|
| Kotpad cloth | [Kotpad](../handlooms/kotpad.md) and [Koraput](../places/koraput.md) | Maker, dye process, material, time and attributed design |
| Bandha textiles | [Sambalpuri Bandha](../handlooms/sambalpuri-bandha.md) and [Bargarh weaving](../handlooms/bargarh.md) | Workshop location, technique, product range and route to market |
| Appliqué and painting | [Pipili](../culture/pipili-applique.md) and [Raghurajpur](../culture/raghurajpur-pattachitra.md) | Artist, process, cultural context and image rights |
| Coffee and rice | [Koraput coffee](../food/koraput-coffee.md) and [Kalajeera rice](../food/koraput-kalajeera-rice.md) | Grower or producer, origin, processing, volumes and verified selling channel |
| Markets and institutions | [Boyanika](../handlooms/boyanika.md) | User-selected reference for textile categories, product presentation and buying research; follow the saved reference-use notes |

These links identify research subjects. They do not verify that a particular shop stocks an item, that a producer exports, or that a host serves a regional food.

## Food enterprises deserve their own evidence

A named dish and a named business are different records. Expand the collection with consenting cooks, processors, cooperatives and entrepreneurs. Establish who makes the product, where production occurs, how ingredients are sourced and which claims the business can substantiate. Track dated sales or production only when the units and geographic scope are clear. No verified food-enterprise sales directory is established yet.

## Connect making with the wider economy

Handlooms and food belong alongside manufacturing, logistics, finance and skills. The [industrial production](../statistics/industrial-production.md) and [exports](../trade/merchandise-exports.md) pages provide wider context; company-wide results must not be relabelled as Odisha-only production. [Progress cards](progress.md) separate proposed industrial capacity from realised output.

## The next evidence to seek

Maker income and working conditions, producer ownership, buyer access, production volumes, provenance and a comparable time series. A GI registration history does not certify every seller or establish current registry validity; check the named product and relevant registry before publishing a certification claim.


[^connect-handloom2019]: [Handloom Weavers — Parliament reply, 13 December 2019](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1596372).


## Connected reading

- [Odisha progress: what the evidence shows](progress.md) — Separate new industrial announcements from measured production.
- [Koraput: landscape, makers and everyday enterprise](../places/koraput.md) — Explore coffee and textiles through a regional profile.
- [Sambalpur–Bargarh: cloth, communities and regional enterprise](../places/sambalpur-bargarh.md) — Explore textile-linked places while preserving district boundaries.
- [Craft Livelihoods](../statistics/craft-livelihoods.md) — Read the census definitions behind the weaver and allied-worker counts.

[People and creations](../people/people-and-creations.md), [garments and markets](../handlooms/garments-and-markets.md), and [rasagola economics](../economy/rasagola-and-sweets.md) extend the collection through named contributions and scoped economic questions.

# Odisha progress: what the evidence shows

A promising project can have several different kinds of evidence. Read the status next to the number. These cards retain the source’s observation date; they are not live dashboards or a claim that every project has passed through every stage.

**Planned** describes an intention or target. **Approved** records an administrative decision. **Operating** needs direct dated evidence of activity. **Measured results** need a defined outcome and period. Installed capacity and reported project completion are additional evidence categories: neither automatically establishes operation or impact.

There is no generic progress percentage or statewide investment total here. “Not established in the saved evidence” means unknown, not zero. Existing observation dates are retained; this collection does not recheck every original release.


## Homestays: an ambition to track

Status: **planned**.

**450 homestay units** — New homestay development target. 2025 scheme; validity through 31 March 2030; Odisha.[^homestay-scheme2025]

The target creates a programme to follow; it is not operating inventory.

Still to establish: Approvals under this scheme; Units open and taking bookings; Room-nights, disbursements and net host income.

[Read the underlying record](../statistics/homestays.md).

## Semiconductors: approval is a dated milestone

Status: **approved**.

**2 projects** — Odisha projects approved in August 2025 ISM decision. 2025-08-12; Odisha.[^legacy-ism]

The August 2025 ISM decision approved two named Odisha projects. Approval does not establish production or hiring.

Still to establish: Commissioning and commercial operations; Realised capital spending; Actual output and employment.

[Read the underlying record](../journeys/semiconductors.md).

## Bhubaneswar: reported project completion

Status: **reported completion**.

**31 projects** — Completed SCM projects. 2026-03-01; Bhubaneswar.[^weekly-smart-mar2026]

**32 projects** — Total SCM projects. 2026-03-01; Bhubaneswar.[^weekly-smart-mar2026]

31 of 32 Smart Cities Mission projects were reported completed at this snapshot. Completion does not establish that every service is operating reliably.

Still to establish: Operating-service verification; Maintenance, usage and resident outcomes.

[Read the underlying record](../journeys/smart-cities.md).

## Rourkela: reported project completion

Status: **reported completion**.

**73 projects** — Completed SCM projects. 2026-03-01; Rourkela.[^weekly-smart-mar2026]

**75 projects** — Total SCM projects. 2026-03-01; Rourkela.[^weekly-smart-mar2026]

73 of 75 Smart Cities Mission projects were reported completed at this snapshot. This is a project-count measure, not a liveability score.

Still to establish: Operating-service verification; Maintenance, usage and resident outcomes.

[Read the underlying record](../journeys/smart-cities.md).

## Rare earths: installed capacity, output still to establish

Status: **installed capacity**.

**11,200 tonnes per annum** — Installed mixed rare-earth chloride capacity. Plant page checked 2026-09-27; capacity effective date unspecified; OSCOM, Odisha.[^journey-irel-reep]

The OSCOM plant page states installed mixed rare-earth chloride capacity. The source does not establish the capacity effective date, current utilisation or actual annual output.

Still to establish: Dated operational status; Production and capacity utilisation; Odisha-attributable sales and jobs.

[Read the underlying record](../journeys/rare-earths.md).

## Debrigarh: reported community participation

Status: **reported activity**.

**More than 150 community members** — Community ecotourism engagement. As reported 20 August 2026; reference date unspecified; Debrigarh Wildlife Sanctuary.[^debrigarh-nie-20260820]

The dated press report attributes community engagement to the local ecotourism programme. It is not a primary payroll roster or a permanent-job count.

Still to establish: Primary dated roster and employment definition; Pay and household net income; Measured conservation outcomes.

[Read the underlying record](../places/debrigarh-hirakud.md).

[^homestay-scheme2025]: [Odisha Homestay Establishment Scheme 2025 — Gazette 5549](https://dot.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-01/5549%20TOURISM%20%20Deptt_0.pdf).

[^legacy-ism]: [Union Cabinet approval: semiconductor units](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2155459&lang=2&reg=3).

[^weekly-smart-mar2026]: [Smart Cities Mission — Rajya Sabha question 2600](https://www.sansad.in/getFile/annex/270/AU2600_vR0ZFk.pdf?source=pqars).

[^journey-irel-reep]: [OSCOM Rare Earth Extraction Plant](https://www.irel.co.in/en-GB/oscom-rare-earth-extraction-plant).

[^debrigarh-nie-20260820]: [Debrigarh infrastructure and community engagement, 20 August 2026](https://www.newindianexpress.com/amp/story/states/odisha/2026/Aug/20/odishas-debrigarh-wildlife-sanctuary-witness-rise-in-visitors-upgraded-infrastructure-gave-push-to-it).


## Connected reading

- [Odisha’s rare-earth journey](../journeys/rare-earths.md) — Read plant capacity with its missing production and utilisation measures.
- [Odisha’s semiconductor journey](../journeys/semiconductors.md) — Keep approvals, proposed capacity and actual production distinct.
- [Debrigarh and Hirakud](../places/debrigarh-hirakud.md) — Retain the press attribution and unknown employment definitions.

# Boita Bandana: honouring the maritime trader

## Sourced knowledge

In Boita Bandana, miniature boats carrying lamps are set afloat in remembrance of maritime journeys. A 2025 Ministry of Culture account connects this practice with Bali Jatra in Cuttack, a festival commemorating trade and cultural exchange between Odisha and Southeast Asia, particularly Bali.[^maritime-culture-2025]

## Editorial interpretation

“A culture that honours its traders” is a defensible contemporary framing of this remembrance. “A celebration of entrepreneurial courage” can be used as our interpretation, rather than as a claim about the festival’s single original purpose.

The ritual carries cultural and devotional meanings as well. Neither participation nor commemoration measures how entrepreneurial all residents are.

## Connect it to action

Use the [Paradip event](../trade/paradip-bridge.md) for a documented institutional connection and [Bali Jatra commerce](../trade/baliyatra-commerce.md) for an attributed present-day sales measure.

[Bali Jatra](bali-yatra.md) · [Campaign](../stories/trading-culture-next-chapter.md)

[^maritime-culture-2025]: [Bali Jatra commemorates rich maritime heritage and culture of Odisha](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2100365)

# Mahima Dharma and Bhima Bhoi

**Bhima Bhoi provides a connection between faith, literature and concern for human suffering.** In a [2 March 2024 address](https://presidentofindia.nic.in/press_releases/president-india-addresses-meeting-mahima-cult), the President described Mahima Gosein as the movement’s initiator and Bhima Bhoi’s poems, songs and speeches as expressions of equality. This is evidence of a public interpretation, not a complete religious history.

The repository already contains a literary introduction based on Sitakant Mahapatra’s *Bhima Bhoi*, published by Sahitya Akademi. Its saved inspection records uncertainty in biography (pp. 1–2), Khaliapali (pp. 12–13) and compassion (pp. 27–28). We reuse that bounded capture rather than create an independently verified duplicate. [Monograph](https://sahitya-akademi.gov.in/pdf/Bhima-Bhoi.pdf).

Next: source Mahima Swami’s chronology, the meaning of Alekh/formless divinity, Joranda and Khaliapali, orders and living practices; identify editions of *Stuti Chintamani* and credited English translations. Exact birth, blindness and community-background accounts require reconciliation. No follower total, contemporary ritual availability or invented interview is provided.

The canonical website narrative remains in the project’s `kb/research/voices/collection.json`; this page adds the religious-history research scope, rather than replacing that literary entry.

[Related reading](../history/buddhist-learning.md) — Offers comparative reading about distinct religious and learning traditions; no common origin or doctrinal equivalence is asserted.
