verification_scope: Source-specific research; indexed-only passages distinguished from direct retrieval. Local/Odia review and media permissions pending.
body:
# Pala and its culture

Pala belongs at the meeting point of performed poetry, musical storytelling and community life. A 2012 festival account connects these ballad traditions with literature, rhythm, humour and epic narratives. [Pala and Daskathia Utsav](https://www.narthaki.com/info/rev12/rev1245.html).

## How to begin listening

Listen for the story, the explanation of a verse and the exchange between the lead voice and accompanying performers. The official 2025 Sammilan account explicitly credits singers and Bayaks for communicating Odia poetry. [48th annual state-level Pala Sammilan at Parklane, Kendujhar](https://cm.odisha.gov.in/en/latest-news/participated-48th-annual-state-level-pala-sammilan-organized-parklane-kendujhar). Detailed roles, instruments and local terminology need an attributed demonstration before becoming a performance manual.

## Forms and history: preserve the source’s vocabulary

Dash’s January 2011 article distinguishes **Pothi Pala** performed seated, **Thia Pala** performed standing, and **Badi Pala**, where singers take turns on a stage. These notes come from the indexed passage at printed page 73; direct PDF access failed. [The Socio-Cultural Value of Odia Folkdance: Pala](https://magazines.odisha.gov.in/Orissareview/2011/Jan/engpdf/72-74.pdf).

A full history needs separately examined evidence for Satyanarayana/Satyapir associations, manuscript dates, teacher lineages and later stage practice. Those are research questions here. A devotional origin account cannot supply a verified founding date; older claims of decline do not measure the present condition.

## Performers and repertoire

The 2009 Sangeet Natak Akademi citation recognises **Jagannath Behera** for Pala theatre and names his teachers. The indexed citation is retained with its full-PDF access gap; its historical age and offices must not become present-day claims. [Jagannath Behera — Akademi Award: Pala (Orissa)](https://sangeetnatak.gov.in/public/uploads/awardees/docs/Jagannath_Behera.pdf).

A contemporary report of the 19–21 July 2012 festival at Rabindra Mandap provides these credited examples:

| Performer | Presentation as reported |
|---|---|
| Santilata Sahu | Hanuman’s meditation in Dwapara Yuga |
| Manorama Panda | Naga Jyoti |
| Kumudini Patel | Sasirekha Parinaya |
| Madanamohana Jena and troupe | Papamochan Yajna |
| Laxman Charan Rout and troupe | Mahadani Ajigarta |

[Pala and Daskathia Utsav](https://www.narthaki.com/info/rev12/rev1245.html). These are dated performance credits, not a complete artist directory. The women performers deserve their own researched biographies. Keep Pala and Daskathia distinct even when a festival presents both.

## A living archive and a dated gathering

The [Shree Jagannath Pala Research Foundation](https://www.sjprf.in/) offers routes to performer material and documentary notices. Its [Pala Kabita catalogue](https://sjprf.in/index.php/pala-kabita) records author attributions, including Bhagabata Bandana by Sarat Chandra Dash. These are useful discovery routes; recordings, editions, translations and rights need item-level checks.

The Chief Minister’s office dates its report of the **48th annual state-level Pala Sammilan in Kendujhar to 28 December 2025**. [48th annual state-level Pala Sammilan at Parklane, Kendujhar](https://cm.odisha.gov.in/en/latest-news/participated-48th-annual-state-level-pala-sammilan-organized-parklane-kendujhar). This establishes a reported gathering and edition number; attendance, artist totals, payments and current booking availability remain unknown.

## Story opportunity

**An evening where poetry becomes performance.** Follow a named artist from choosing a text to explaining it to an audience; credit accompanying artists and the community that hosts the performance. This is an editorial proposal, not a filmed or interviewed story.

## Next research

Recover the two government PDFs; verify performer biographies and women’s participation through independent records; catalogue named texts and legally viewable recordings; document instruments, apprenticeship and community settings. Add dated troupe, funding or earnings statistics only when units and coverage are clear. No local interview, Odia review, verified event calendar or media licence is claimed.

title: Tantric traditions: sites, texts and interpretations
description: Tantric traditions: sites, texts and interpretations — sourced starting record and further questions.
body:
# Tantric traditions: sites, texts and interpretations

**Begin with identifiable places and attributed scholarship.** Odisha Tourism describes Hirapur’s Chausathi Yogini temple as circular and open to the sky, dates it to the ninth century, and attributes it to Queen Hiradevi. These are the tourism publisher’s historical attributions, pending archaeological and epigraphic review. [Official description](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/discover/attractions/temples-monuments/chausathi-yogini.html).

Its reference to Ranipur-Jharial opens a second site for research. We do not adopt its nationwide surviving-temple total, current event calendar or speculative explanations of ritual practice.

Research should distinguish Yogini/Shakta and Shaiva traditions from Buddhist Vajrayana; a shared word such as tantra does not make them one religion. Follow named deities, dated sculptures, inscriptions, texts and scholarly interpretations. Explore documented connections with Jagannath traditions without assuming a single origin. Avoid sensational descriptions or invented secret practices.

Next: ASI monument records, Odisha State Museum catalogues, dated Ranipur-Jharial research, and specialist accounts of Hirapur. Contemporary practice requires attributed practitioner knowledge; none has been collected in this batch.

[Related reading](../history/buddhist-learning.md) — Points to questions about Buddhist Vajrayana while keeping Buddhist and Yogini/Shakta histories distinct.

# Odisha’s universities: institutions and evidence

**Compare institutions by their role, legal category and dated evidence.** The [Higher Education Department directory](https://dhe.odisha.gov.in/en/universities/list-of-univerisities-in-odisha) supplies the following starting selection, not a best-university league table or a complete statewide census.

| Directory category | Selected institutions to profile |
| --- | --- |
| State public | Utkal, Ravenshaw, Sambalpur, Berhampur, OUAT, Utkal University of Culture, Odisha State Open University, National Law University Odisha |
| Central | Central University of Odisha |
| State private | Centurion, Sri Sri, Birla Global, ASBM, GIET, Silicon |
| Deemed to be university | KIIT, Siksha ‘O’ Anusandhan, KISS |

Deemed status is a legal category; it does not itself establish government ownership. Directory inclusion does not verify current programme approval, admissions, accreditation or every institutional name change. IIT, NIT, NISER, IISER and AIIMS coverage needs a separate institution-type check.

**One dated finding:** NIRF’s **2025 University category** places **Siksha ‘O’ Anusandhan 15th** (63.14) and **KIIT 17th** (62.87). These are India ranks in that category, not ranks among all institutions or subject-specific outcomes. [Original ranking table](https://www.nirfindia.org/Rankings/2025/UniversityRanking.html).

The attempted 2026 table could not be retrieved. These numbers are explicitly 2025; no latest-ranking claim is made.

Next: UGC identities and notifications, establishment versus university-status dates, department strengths, research output, access, graduate outcomes and comparable multi-year NIRF data. Keep score, rank, category and year together; do not infer growth from rank movements alone.

body:
# Forest products: household use, markets and livelihoods

**The central question is how forest knowledge and produce support everyday life and paid work.** Keep foods connected to the wider non-timber forest-products economy without calling every product food.

| Research group | What to document |
| --- | --- |
| Fruits, kernels, flowers and honey | Identity, use, season, preservation, supply origin and food-processing evidence |
| Leaves and leaf products | Sal-leaf collection, plate-making, labour, local buyers and processing; examine other leaf identities separately |
| Oilseeds, gums, resins and lac | Product and grade, actual end uses, processing yields and prices |
| Bamboo, cane, fibres and brooms | Material, maker, end product and commercial channel |
| Kendu leaves | A non-food commodity used as bidi wrappers; separate leaf trade from any fruit entry |

These groups define research coverage. Inclusion does not establish present procurement, sustainable supply, exports or proven medicinal effects. The TDCCOL product page is currently a partially captured discovery lead, not a verified current buying list.

## Follow value through each transaction

A proposed reporting chain is **collection → household use or local sale → aggregation → processing → retail or export**. Verify actual buyers before claiming a product follows that chain. Record procurement separately from sales, and collector receipts separately from turnover and net earnings. Prices require date, place, grade, moisture and unit. Published support prices do not prove procurement at that price.

[The first market checkpoint](../statistics/forest-products.md) saves a kendu series and one honey-processing capacity observation. It is not an estimate of Odisha's entire forest-food market. [Forest foods](../food/forest-foods.md) retains household and culinary context; [history](../history/forest-livelihoods.md) provides dated evidence rather than invented ancient origins.

## Next evidence to obtain

Product-level TDCCOL/Van Dhan procurement and realised sales; collector payments and costs; women-led groups and named community enterprises; seasonal haat prices; storage loss and processing yields; state-origin export quantities. Export promotion, an online listing or an overseas buyer mention alone does not establish measured shipments. For land, collection rights and ecological effects, use current primary decisions and location-specific studies.

[Structured research register](../references/data/forest-products.json).

[Related reading](../food/forest-foods.md) — Connects commodity research to household uses and ingredient identities; forest origin requires its own evidence.

[Related reading](../history/forest-livelihoods.md) — Adds dated institutional and community-study context without dating the origin of traditions.

[Related reading](../statistics/forests.md) — Provides land-cover context; forest area does not estimate product yields or household income.

[Related reading](../economy/mining.md) — Connects research on land and livelihoods; no causal effect of a named mine is asserted.

title: Odisha’s GDP story: scale, momentum and meaning
description: Odisha’s GDP story: scale, momentum and meaning — research and reuse notes.
body:
# Odisha’s GDP story: scale, momentum and meaning

The most useful economic narrative connects the size of the economy to visible sectors and places. Lead with a clear, dated number and then show what it represents.

## Opening evidence

The preserved survey records give **₹9.88 lakh crore nominal GSDP** and **7.9% real GSDP growth** for FY2025–26, both advance estimates. These are two different measures: [economic size](../evidence/e02.md) and [inflation-adjusted annual growth](../evidence/e01.md). They can sit side by side if labelled properly.

## Suggested message

“Odisha’s next chapter is taking shape.” Follow it with the economic-size number, its estimate label, and a sequence covering ports, production, food, services and people. Treat the phrase as campaign language rather than a statistical finding.

## A richer proof sequence

Use [construction’s five-year real growth](construction.md), [fisheries production](comparison-01-fisheries.md) and [Paradip cargo](comparison-05-port-logistics.md) as distinct stories. Their measures must stay separate: economic value added, physical output and port throughput. They cannot be added into a single “growth” total.

The [industry growth collection](index.md) retains complete six-year sector series so the campaign can use both the positive endpoint comparison and a truthful chart. A changing trajectory is more informative than an invented uninterrupted boom.

## Publication controls

Use a common vintage and price basis for any India comparison. The state survey’s national comparator and later national estimates are not automatically comparable: see [survey comparator](../evidence/e04.md) and [later national estimate](../evidence/e05.md). Do not call nominal expansion real growth. Do not turn per-capita income into a claim about every household. Announced investments and jobs remain announcements until completion is established.

The nominal ten-year tripling angle from earlier work needs its historical starting value added as an independently locatable record before it becomes a website headline.

## Fresh series expansion

The [economic-size and income atlas](../statistics/economic-size-and-income.md) records the current-price 2018–19 to 2025–26 series with revision/advance-estimate labels and explicit lakh-to-crore conversion. It supports the saved five-year nominal comparison, not a real-growth or ten-year claim.

body:
# Homestays: government support and policy history

A hosted home can connect accommodation spending with local food, crafts and work. Odisha’s support programme creates an opportunity to develop those connections; household income and benefits to makers still need measurement.

## What the 2025 scheme provides

The Gazette defines family-hosted accommodation around the owner’s residence. Its financial route supports selected new units in notified rural areas; other units have a separate non-financial route. The notified framework offers up to **50% of eligible fixed capital investment excluding land**, limited to **₹2.5 lakh per lettable room**, four rooms and **₹10 lakh per unit**. Payment is conditional and staged: 50%, 15%, 15% and 20%, with later booking-night thresholds of 15, 30 and 45 per room. These are historical source provisions, not amounts already paid.[^homestay-scheme2025]

Support also includes promotion, training, mentoring and digital visitor management. The budget window ends FY2028–29, while scheme validity runs to 31 March 2030 unless changed. The programme supersedes the 2021 scheme.[^homestay-scheme2025]

## Policy sequence and currentness

| Date | What is established | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| 24/29 November 2025 | Notification/Gazette publication of the 2025 scheme | Later amendments must be read with it |
| 5 March 2026 | Go Homestay launch reported on 6 March | Event report; not adoption figures[^homestay-launch-mar2026] |
| April–May 2026 | Official guidelines index lists an amendment and Cycle-1 targets | Linked PDFs could not be retrieved in this run[^homestay-guideline-index] |
| 19 May 2026 | First-cycle targets described in reporting | Target, not achievement[^homestay-cycle1-may2026] |
| 5 August 2026 | New Homestay Scheme entry in official Gazette archive | Metadata checked; underlying text unavailable[^homestay-gazette-aug2026] |

A regulatory publisher reports a July amendment concerning residency within the Block and a Rayagada GP correction. This remains a **discovery lead**, because the Gazette text was not obtained. Do not use the original GP-residence clause or this secondary summary as definitive current application guidance.[^homestay-amendment-lead]

## Digital support: what exists versus what is measured

The public Go Homestay address is saved, but its page returned no readable dashboard data in this run.[^homestay-go-portal] OCAC’s app listing describes application tracking, inspections, incentives, visitor records and reporting. These advertised functions are useful source leads; they were not tested in an authenticated account. App downloads are not counts of hosts, bookings or approved units.[^homestay-go-app]

## National programmes are a separate layer

The national parliamentary reply describes a 1,000-homestay tribal-development intervention and national credit support. Those are India-level programmes, not an Odisha allocation. National classification, state registration, marketing-platform listings and financial-benefit selection need separate labels.[^homestay-nidhi2025]

## Connections to document next

Record host consent, a stable property ID, operating status, room count and date before recommending a stay. A regional food tradition does not prove that a host serves it; a nearby craft centre does not prove a commercial relationship. Research actual meals, guide services, maker visits and purchases through attributed local accounts. No booking recommendation follows from scheme eligibility alone.

- [Homestay data](../statistics/homestays.md) — Read targets, registries and market listings with their distinct meanings.
- [Food collection](../food/index.md) and [handlooms](../handlooms/index.md) — Potential local experiences to investigate with hosts and makers.
- [Classification](../methods/content-classification.md) — Keep topic association separate from demonstrated commercial links.

[Economy](../subjects/economy.md) · [Governance](../subjects/governance.md) · [People](../subjects/people.md)

[^homestay-scheme2025]: [Odisha Homestay Establishment Scheme 2025 — Gazette 5549](https://dot.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-01/5549%20TOURISM%20%20Deptt_0.pdf).

[^homestay-guideline-index]: [Odisha Tourism guidelines: amendments and Cycle 1 targets](https://dot.odisha.gov.in/en/guidelines).

[^homestay-gazette-aug2026]: [Tourism Gazette archive: Homestay Scheme entry, 5 August 2026](https://egazette.odisha.gov.in/extraordinary_archival_dept/70/1).

[^homestay-nidhi2025]: [One India, One Registration Initiative under NIDHI Portal](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2155162&lang=2&reg=48).

[^homestay-go-portal]: [Go Homestay official portal](https://gohomestay.odisha.gov.in/).

[^homestay-go-app]: [Go Homestay Portal — OCAC app listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?hl=en_IN&id=com.aashdit.gohomestay).

[^homestay-launch-mar2026]: [State launches Go Homestay portal](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bhubaneswar/state-launches-go-homestay-portal/articleshow/129108175.cms).

[^homestay-cycle1-may2026]: [From Deomali to Daringbadi, homestays get a push](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bhubaneswar/from-deomali-to-daringbadi-homestays-get-a-push/articleshow/131184349.cms).

[^homestay-market-jan2025]: [Homestay count grows manifold in Odisha but local experience missing](https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/odisha/2025/Jan/04/homestay-count-grows-manifold-in-odisha-but-local-experience-missing).

[^homestay-amendment-lead]: [Reported July 2026 homestay eligibility amendment](https://teamleaseregtech.com/updates/article/59065/odisha-tourism-amendment-to-homestay-establishment-scheme-2025/).

## Policy reconciliation checkpoint · 1 October 2026

The [official portal](https://gohomestay.odisha.gov.in/) now supplies a readable area table and notice list. Seven distinct titles include “11436”, “Ammendment 17.08.26”, an application-deadline extension and a Rayagada correction. The title date is not independently verified as the notification or effective date. The carousel repeats notices; repeats are not new releases.

The April amendment and Cycle-1 official PDF downloads timed out. Portal document buttons did not produce readable originals in this session. RES-008 therefore remains blocked for text retrieval, with retry on 8 October. Its policy and geographic conflicts are not resolved by the availability of a portal table. The portal still displays GP-residence wording; the July secondary lead reports broader Block residency. Do not give definitive applicant guidance from either alone.

### From a place list to livelihood evidence

RES-009 begins with the 2025 scheme’s own reporting route: printed pp. 27–28 describe programme monitoring; the blank annual declaration at p. 49 asks for operation/closure status, rooms and beds, guest-nights, revenue, occupancy, family/local staff and subsidy received. This establishes potential administrative evidence, not that returns were filed or outcomes achieved. Parsed text was read; no new visual PDF verification is claimed.

Next retrieve aggregate completed returns or departmental progress reports with their reporting period, responding-property denominator, cancellations/closures and revision dates. Guest-nights cannot silently become room-nights; gross revenue cannot become net household income. The [monitoring record](../references/data/homestay-research.json) keeps every unavailable outcome null. The nine missing outcome measures remain open.

## Operating evidence checkpoint · 1 October 2026

World Tourism Day coverage supplies a new lead but conflicting quantities: [Odisha Connect](https://odishaconnect.com/odisha-celebrates-world-tourism-day-2026-with-digital-innovation-and-community-led-tourism/) reports 176 provisional-registration beneficiaries in an indexed passage; [OdishaBytes](https://odishabytes.com/odisha-signs-pacts-to-promote-homestay-heritage-adventure-tourism/amp/) says 17 in its directly read closing paragraph. The event is 27 September 2026. Both counts are held pending an original departmental release/register, outside the headline statistics. The reports may draw on the same event announcement.

OdishaBytes also reports an SBI financing MoU. Its signed terms, loan approvals and disbursements were not obtained. An agreement is not realised lending. No active-property census, completed compliance returns, occupancy or host-income data was recovered in this bounded search. Unknown remains unknown.

[Community ecotourism evidence](../statistics/ecotourism.md) now supplies a separately scoped programme income/visitor series; it does not fill homestay operating gaps.

title: Odisha mining: minerals, industry and people
description: Odisha mining: minerals, industry and people — scoped evidence and research questions.

sources.title: Monthly Statistics of Mineral Production, March 2025
PMKKKY and District Mineral Foundations in Odisha: Report 7 of 2026

body:
# Odisha mining: minerals, industry and people

**Mining needs a connected encyclopedia section.** The editorial question is: how does mineral wealth become lasting value for Odisha? Answer it through production, processing, public money, working lives and the places affected.

| Angle | Question to answer |
| --- | --- |
| Minerals and geology | Which minerals occur where, with what dated reserve/resource classifications? |
| Production and national position | How have coal, iron ore, bauxite, chromite, manganese and other minerals changed over five and ten years? |
| Processing and manufacturing | How much ore is beneficiated, refined or made into metal and finished products inside Odisha? |
| Revenue and public finances | What do royalties, auction premiums and other receipts contribute, and how volatile are they? |
| Mining-area development | What do DMF projects deliver in health, water, schooling and livelihoods? |
| Jobs, skills and small businesses | Who works in mines, plants, transport and supplier firms, under what employment conditions? |
| Trade and transport | Where do minerals and metals go through railways, ports and domestic supply chains? |
| Land, rights and communities | How do acquisition, resettlement, consent, forest rights and local livelihoods affect mining communities? |
| Air, water, forests and health | What do site monitoring records show about dust, water, waste, forests and exposure? |
| Safety and mine closure | What happens during operation, closure and restoration, and what liabilities remain? |
| Ownership and accountability | Who owns and operates each lease; what is its current stage and compliance history? |
| Industrial history and future materials | How did mining towns develop, and what could recycling, research and critical minerals change? |

## Start with the evidence already saved

Reuse the existing [real mining value-added series](mining-and-quarrying.md), [bauxite](comparison-06-mining.md), [coal](comparison-07-mining.md) and [iron-ore comparisons](comparison-08-mining.md). These are imported records with stated vintages, not freshly verified by their inclusion here. Reconcile future captures alongside them without rewriting the frozen ledger.

[The first statistical checkpoint](../statistics/minerals-and-mining.md) adds dated national production shares and mining-area fund evidence. The [rare-earth journey](../journeys/rare-earths.md) already separates OSCOM capacity from proposed expansion.

## District and value-chain research

Build profiles around mineral, mine, operator, district, processing plant and transport route. Candidate geographies for verification include Keonjhar/Kendujhar and Sundargarh, the Sukinda/Jajpur area, Angul–Talcher and the Ib Valley, and bauxite-linked areas of Koraput, Rayagada and Kalahandi. This is a research selection, not a verified deposit or active-mine map. Preserve historical and administrative aliases.

Begin with iron ore → beneficiation/pellets → iron and steel; bauxite → alumina → aluminium → fabrication; chromite → ferrochrome → stainless steel; coal → power and industrial uses. These are research pathways, not verified supplier relationships between particular companies. Link plant-level evidence before drawing arrows on a public map.

## What readers should see

Short mineral explainers, district portraits, credited worker and scientist profiles, five- or ten-year charts, and plant-stage timelines. A public card should carry one takeaway, its year/unit and a source reveal. A mine profile should state whether it is proposed, auctioned, leased, operating, suspended or closed, with an observation date.

Keep useful positive achievements alongside setbacks and unresolved questions. More ore extracted does not on its own establish higher local incomes or better services. Green-mining claims need measured outcomes.

[Structured coverage and evidence pointers](../references/data/mining-programme.json).

[Related reading](../statistics/minerals-and-mining.md) — Connects the broad mining questions to dated national contribution and fund-use measures, without claiming causal local benefits.

[Related reading](../journeys/rare-earths.md) — Reuses the rare-earth processing record while keeping capacity, actual output and proposals separate.

[Related reading](../statistics/industrial-production.md) — Links ore extraction to plant-level output research; mineral and processed-metal quantities must not be summed.

title: Rasagola economics and Odisha’s sweets
description: Rasagola economics and Odisha’s sweets — sourced research, relationships and open questions.

body:
# Rasagola economics and Odisha’s sweets

**Follow a sweet from milk to market.** Rasagola economics can connect dairy farmers, chhena makers, sweet shops, packaging, cold storage, transport, festivals and overseas buyers. This is our research framework; a statewide revenue total has not yet been established.

## Build on the existing sweet records

- [Odisha Rasagola](../food/odisha-rasagola.md): retain the historical GI certificate and distinguish Pahala/Salepur business clusters from the protected product’s statewide geography.
- [Chhena poda](../food/chhena-poda.md): deepen local history, preparation and producer evidence.
- [Chhena jhili](../food/chhena-jhili.md): place-linked Nimapada research.
- [Kendrapara Rasabali](../food/kendrapara-rasabali.md): separate GI record, cultural context and enterprise data.
- [Dhenkanal Magji](../food/dhenkanal-magji.md): names, ingredients, historical record and producer verification.
- [Korakhai](../food/korakhai.md): ritual and place context; commercial output remains to research.

These are existing research records, not a complete sweet inventory. Khaja, chhena gaja, chhena murki and region-specific variants are follow-up candidates whose product descriptions need sources.

## What export evidence currently says

APEDA and the Odisha government displayed **Salepur Rasagolla, Kendrapada Rasabali and Dhenkanal Magaji Ladoo** at their Bhubaneswar agri-export workshop on 25 April 2025. The 27 April release discusses processing, logistics and cold-chain opportunities. This establishes export promotion, **not completed sweet shipments or export revenue**.

## The numbers to collect

| Measure | Required scope |
|---|---|
| Milk and chhena input; sweet output | Producer, period, kg/litres, yield and wastage |
| Sales | Named business or representative survey; domestic and export revenue separate |
| Work and income | Paid workers, family work, seasonality, wages and net income |
| Export shipments | Actual shipment date, producer origin, quantity, value, destination and product identity |
| Costs | Milk, sugar, labour, fuel, packaging, transport and spoilage on the same batch basis |
| Cluster scale | Counted enterprises and sampling method; avoid multiplying a few popular shops by an invented statewide total |

All sweet-specific export quantities, values and destination counts remain unknown in this batch. Overseas online availability is a lead, not proof of an Odisha-origin shipment. Customs categories may aggregate many sweets, and shipments via another state may obscure manufacturing origin. Reconcile these before claiming a global rasagola market size.

A future margin calculator can use explicit user inputs; scenario estimates must remain separate from observed industry statistics. Research lawful shelf-life and packaging evidence from responsible food-science authorities before publishing operational guidance.

[Export-promotion source](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2124747) · [Structured open measures](../references/data/creative-economy.json).

[Odisha Rasagola](../food/odisha-rasagola.md) — Read product identity alongside economic questions; a GI record does not measure industry revenue.

## Rasabali evidence lead · 1 October 2026

The [Rasabali preparation follow-up](../food/kendrapara-rasabali.md) captures the original 2023 GI applicant’s seller/maker claims and the correction that repeats them. Their reference period and method are absent; they remain held leads in [the preparation register](../references/data/food-preparations.json), owned by RES-031. No current employment total, revenue or export estimate has been added.

title: Bela pana: a summer drink and an Odia New Year connection
description: Bela pana: a summer drink and an Odia New Year connection — attributed evidence and preparation scope.

sources.title: Bael Ka Sharbat (Bel Ka Sharbat)(Wood Apple Sharbat)
Celebration of 132nd birth anniversary of Baba Saheb Ambedkar and Odia New Year
Ethnobotanical exploration of wild edible fruits of Balasore district in Odisha, India

body:
# Bela pana: a summer drink and an Odia New Year connection

Bela pana brings ripe bael fruit into Odisha’s summer-drink repertoire. The ingredient is **bela, *Aegle marmelos***. The saved [Balasore fruit study](../sources/food-koli-balasore2020.md), Table 1 row 1, records its pulp in sherbet and squash; row 42 separately identifies kaitha as *Limonia acidissima*. English “wood apple” labels alone should not merge these fruits.

## How one home version is made

[Sasmita Sahoo’s 2021 account](https://rosheighara.wordpress.com/2021/04/16/4-traditional-healthy-drinks-of-odisha/) places Bela pana among summer drinks. Her version uses one bael fruit, five glasses of water, sugar or mishri, and black pepper.

1. Dissolve the sweetener in water.
2. Open the fruit and scoop out its pulp.
3. Work the pulp into the water and separate the seeds.
4. Strain; finish each serving with pepper. Ice is optional in this account.

**Quantity gaps:** glass size and sweetener amount are unspecified. The ingredient list gives a “small tablespoon” of pepper, while the method says a pinch per serving. Keep that discrepancy visible: this is an attributed method, not a calibrated or kitchen-tested Utkal recipe.

## More than one preparation

[Chef Reetu Uday Kugaji’s account](https://chefreetuudaykugaji.com/blog/2023/03/06/bael-ka-sharbat-bel-ka-sharbatwood-apple-sharbat%EF%BF%BC/) describes an Odisha version with pepper, grated coconut, mashed banana and chhena alongside strained bael, water and sugar or jaggery. This is a credited variation, not a rule for every household. Her separate measured sharbat-concentrate recipe is not relabelled as this Bela pana version.

## Summer and Odia New Year

[Fakir Mohan University’s report](https://fmuniversity.nic.in/getdata?dir=InstituteNews&rid=inewsEvent75_15420231681554279989.pdf) documents Bela pana at its **14 April 2023 Odia New Year / Maha Bishuba Sankranti celebration** in Nuapadhi, Balasore. This establishes a specific cultural example, not participation totals or one obligatory festival recipe.

The Balasore field study reports May–June for Bela fruiting within its January 2018–February 2020 survey of five blocks. That source-specific season is not a statewide retail calendar, and an April festival serving does not establish an April local harvest. A government-hosted Odisha Review article on Bela and Pana Sankranti remains a follow-up: its full PDF exceeded the browser fetch limit in this run.

## What to collect next

Record household and district variations, reviewed Odia spelling, fruit size or pulp weight, measured water and sweetness, and an actually tested preparation. A dated vendor sample could document fruit prices, servings per fruit and sales; **current prices, statewide production, drink revenue and exports remain unknown**. No health-treatment or shelf-life claims from the recipe sources are adopted.

## Proposed story treatment

**Odisha’s Best-Kept Secret · A summer glass of bela pana.** Follow the fruit from a tree or market to an attributed household recipe and an evidenced festival setting. This is an editorial proposal; photographs, interviews and market observations have not been produced.


[Everyday food culture](everyday-food-culture.md) — Connects a seasonal fruit drink with household food knowledge and documented preparations.

[Koli fruits](koli-fruits.md) — Connects Bela ingredient identification with source-specific local fruit names; this does not classify Bela as a koli cultivar.

# Odisha’s everyday food culture

A meal can tell a large story through its smallest accompaniments. This collection follows drying, crushing, leaf cooking, seasonal fruit and rice-water preparations, giving everyday knowledge its own place in Utkal. This framing is editorial; the accounts below identify their contributors and limits.

| Food | What the evidence lets us explore |
|---|---|
| [Badi chura](badi-chura.md) | Condiment; preserving and crushing. |
| [Sukhua](sukhua.md) | Preserved ingredient family; drying and cooking. |
| [Tala pitha](tala-pitha.md) | Seasonal preparation family; ripe palm fruit preparations. |
| [Torani and torani pani](torani.md) | Rice-water food and drink terminology; meal liquids. |
| [Torani kanji](torani-kanji.md) | Cooked dish; boiling and tempering. |
| [Patra poda chatu](chatu-patrapoda.md) | Reuse the existing mushroom entry: leaf wrapping and mustard-seasoned cooking. |

## Tala khaja: a seed-food lead

Ahimanikya clarified on 1 October 2026 that “khaja is seed produce.” Preserve **tala khaja** as the supplied palm-seed food name. The exact seed stage, preparation and local/Odia spelling remain to be documented. Do not merge it with the khaja pastry or automatically equate it to tala gaja or tala saja. A Commons photograph labelled tala gaja in Baleswar is a discovery lead only: its full page could not be retrieved in this run.

## A useful way to tell the story

Begin with the ingredient and the hands that prepare it, then show its place in a meal. Add the local name, season, district or community only when evidenced. Producer livelihoods belong beside culinary practice; state totals, exports and nutrition claims need their own evidence.

Next collection candidates are saga preparations, ambula and other souring ingredients, chutneys, seasonal greens and household preservation. Search existing records before creating identities. Local participation and Odia review remain pending.

body:
# Forest foods: knowledge, seasons and everyday life

**Build this collection around ingredients, the people who know them and the seasons in which they are used.** Household food, local exchange and commercial trade deserve separate evidence.

## Reuse the food identities already documented

[Koli fruits](koli-fruits.md) already records botanical and local-name distinctions, including chara, jammu and several kinds of bara. That collection is a starting point for location-specific forest-food research, not proof that every market fruit is wild harvested. [Ou khatta](ou-khatta.md) and [bela pana](bela-pana.md) preserve attributed preparations; record cultivated, garden and wild origins separately when known. [Chatu patrapoda](chatu-patrapoda.md) connects food with leaf cooking, but a recipe does not establish a mushroom's wild origin or edible species identity.

## What households keep matters too

Mishra and Pradhan's 2018 publication describes 120 households in six villages of Patana and Bansapal, Kendujhar. Its abstract reports that **38.09% of collected non-timber forest products were consumed and 61.91% sold**. This includes edible and non-edible materials; it is not a diet share. The fieldwork year is unspecified in the abstract, and the sample cannot represent all Odisha. [Study abstract](https://ideas.repec.org/a/ags/injagm/399613.html).

## Product stories to build

Document fruits and kernels, flowers, honey, edible leaves and shoots, tubers and identified edible fungi. These are research groups, not a verified list of edible Odisha species. Each entry needs the local name and language, identified species and plant part, place, season, community-attributed uses, preservation or preparation account, and whether supply is wild, cultivated or mixed. Do not collapse one community's knowledge into a single statewide tradition.

[Preparation and variation](preparation-and-variation.md) remains the recipe home. Add reliable, attributed versions there when available; do not publish identification-dependent wild-food instructions from a common name alone. Monetary sales cannot capture every food's household or cultural value.

[Markets and non-food products](../economy/forest-products.md) · [Historical evidence](../history/forest-livelihoods.md).

body:
# Koli: Odisha’s local fruit names and varieties

Koli is a useful local-language doorway into Odisha’s fruit diversity. The names below span several botanical groups; they are not cultivars of a single fruit. Preserve the place and source behind each name.

## A first selection

| Local name in the source | Botanical name as reported |
|---|---|
| Bara koli | *Ziziphus mauritiana* |
| Jangli bara koli | *Ziziphus nummularia* |
| Kantai / Kana koli | *Ziziphus oenoplia* |
| Tina koli | *Ziziphus rugosa* |
| Jammu koli | *Syzygium cumini* |
| Nara koli | *Phyllanthus acidus* |
| Karanda / Anku koli | *Carissa carandas* |
| Bhaincha koli | *Flacourtia indica* |
| Chara koli | *Buchanania lanzan* |
| Pharsa koli | *Grewia asiatica* |
| Guala koli | *Cordia dichotoma* |
| Lakhan koli | *Uvaria hamiltonii* |

Most mappings come from Noor and Satapathy’s [Balasore field study](https://www.botanyjournals.com/assets/archives/2020/vol5issue3/5-3-106-999.pdf), Table 1. Lakhan comes from [RPRC’s garden account](https://rprcbbsr.in/researchanddevelopment/conservation/wildediblefruitgarden). Botanical names retain the publications’ usage. The [structured register](../references/data/koli-fruits.json) keeps row locations and source-specific seasons.

## One local name can point to different plants

RPRC uses **Khirakoli** for *Carissa spinarum*. The Balasore table labels *Manilkara hexandra* **Khira-koli** and calls *Carissa spinarum* **Anka-koli**. This overlap needs local spelling and specimen checks; the records remain separate.

## Food, markets and conservation

RPRC connects wild fruits with village markets and maintains a conservation collection. Its institutional holdings do not establish how many koli varieties Odisha has. The Balasore study records pickle uses for bara, pharsa and guala; exact preparations require credited recipe evidence.

[Patra and Basak’s 2020 pectin study](https://www.foodandnutritionjournal.org/volume8number2/physicochemical-characterization-of-pectin-extracted-from-six-wild-edible-fruits-in-odisha-india/) supplies another Karanda koli account and a possible processing-research connection. Laboratory findings are not evidence of sales or exports.

## Next evidence

Add reviewed Odia spellings, locality, fruit photographs with rights, taste descriptions, food uses and attributed recipes. Verify named cultivars separately from species. Collect dated market observations before describing availability or prices. This is a cultural research index, not a guide for identifying something picked in the wild. No medicinal claims or general fermentation/storage advice are adopted.

## Story opportunity

**The small fruits that mark the seasons.** A proposed series could follow a verified fruit from its local name and harvest to a household preparation and village market. Photographs, interviews and recipes have not yet been produced.

[Everyday food culture](everyday-food-culture.md) — Connects fruit names and seasonal food knowledge with the existing everyday-food collection; local names do not establish identical botanical species.

[Ekamra Kanan](../places/ekamra-kanan.md) — RPRC’s botanical collections, cactus-claim scope and connections to wild fruits.

body:
# Odisha Rasagola

**A sweet can carry a place’s memory.** Follow rasagola through Odisha’s ritual life, literary references and sweet-making communities.

## A homecoming in Puri

OSIC describes rasagola’s offering to Lakshmi on Jagannath’s behalf at Niladri Bije and cites the temple’s 1955 Record of Rights. The ritual belongs to devotional tradition; it is not a dated account of invention.[^rasagola-osic]

## A thread through Odia literature

The same publication identifies a rasagola reference in Balaram Das’s Dandi Ramayana. We have inspected OSIC’s account, not independently collated the original passage or dated its earliest manuscript witness.[^rasagola-osic]

## Meet the places that keep making it

A travelogue hosted by Odisha Tourism describes Pahala’s roadside sweet market between Bhubaneswar and Cuttack and mentions Salepur’s rasagola tradition. These are connections for future maker-led stories; the account concerns a 2019 visit, not verified present-day hours, prices or vendor quality.[^rasagola-market-travelogue]

Ask a maker what they learned, who taught them, and what they want the next generation to remember. Photograph the making with permission. Record their account as testimony, with their name and date, rather than treating one shop’s story as the history of every rasagola.

## A named Odisha identity

The GI Registry lists Odisha Rasagola under application 612, with a certificate dated 29 July 2019. Odisha’s named product and cultural connections deserve explicit recognition. Registration alone does not settle every competing account of the sweet’s first invention.[^gi-rasagola]

## The filed historical statement

The registry’s GI Journal 116, dated 27 March 2019, was retrieved and its page 10 visually inspected on 1 October 2026. It cites the temple Record of Rights, Part III, under the Law Department notification of 12 October 1955, and identifies the Ayodhya Kanda hospitality episode in Dandi Ramayana. This is the application’s statement of evidence, not an inspection of the original record or a critical literary edition. The journal is available through “612 - GI - Journal Copy - 27-03-2019” in the registry document list.[^gi-rasagola]

A separately sourced, author-released public-domain Pahala rasagola photograph now supports the website feature. Its image metadata is recorded in [the food collection](collection.json); a photograph does not establish an origin claim.

## Research still to do

Inspect the cited temple record and a critical edition of Dandi Ramayana; record editions, page references and dates. Add consented maker interviews from Pahala and Salepur, with properly licensed images. Keep ritual, documentary evidence and oral testimony distinct.

## Preparation and variations · 1 October 2026

The menu describes elephant-apple chutney tempered with panch phutana. [Chef TZac: Odia cuisine is an evolved cuisine](https://apps.odishatourism.gov.in/blog-detail/chef-tzac-odia-cuisine-is-an-evolved-cuisine), Odia Experience menu, accompaniment paragraph. Mansita Mishra’s 27 November 2019 account of a chef and restaurant menu; contemporary interpretation, not a universal or current menu.

The Odisha summary lists Ouu khatta, but a later elephant-apple/jaggery entry is labelled Assam. That geography is unresolved. [Regional Cuisine of India, BHM-602AT](https://uou.ac.in/sites/default/files/slm/BHM-602AT.pdf), Printed p.131 / PDF p.131, Odisha summary; p.292 / PDF p.292, Oou Khatta entry. University teaching reference; one described version, not a definitive formula.

**Still to verify:** Keep the university’s Assam label visible; do not turn it into an Odisha regional recipe or an exclusivity claim. Odia and local review remain pending.

[Preparation collection](preparation-and-variation.md) — Compare techniques and attributed versions across the existing food entries.

## A cook’s two versions and a remembered meal · 1 October 2026

Sasmita identifies Odisha as her home state and documents two versions. Her 2017 sweet preparation uses boiled fruit, jaggery or sugar, seed tempering, ginger and coconut.[^food-ou-sasmita2017] Her 2019 version uses mustard–cumin paste and panch phoron with jaggery; it omits onion and garlic.[^food-ou-sasmita2019] These are two accounts from one author, not independent surveys or district recipes.

Julie Acharya Ray’s 2014 family memoir remembers ou khatta in her mother’s Kartik meal.[^food-ou-ray2014] This connects the dish to one household’s seasonal memory without claiming uniform observance across Odisha. Compare [Dalma](dalma.md). The attributed relish account offers rice and dalma as a serving combination; meal context, not universal ritual prescription.

The university’s Assam-labelled passage remains unresolved. These attributed Odisha accounts do not establish exclusive origin or make that other label an error. Recipe testing, local/Odia review, precise district distribution, current availability and economic totals remain unknown.

# Pitha: a collection, not one dish

Odisha’s pitha repertoire includes pan-cooked, boiled, baked and fried preparations.[^food-tourism]

For the website, make this a browsable collection. Begin with [chakuli](chakuli.md), [poda](poda-pitha.md), [enduri](enduri-pitha.md), [sijha manda](manda-pitha.md), [kakara](kakara-pitha.md) and [arisa](arisa-pitha.md). These are examples, not an inventory of all Odia pitha.

## Editorial proposal

“How many ways can a home say welcome?” is a stronger opening than a large unverified dish count. Each page should show a whole serving, a texture close-up and the maker’s hands. Let the cook identify the occasion, ingredients and variation. A six-part series can introduce one preparation at a time and end with a tasting spread.

## Recipe research template

Capture local name and approved spelling; place; contributor credit and consent; ingredient quantities; preparation method; household variation; occasion; serving context; photography rights; and dietary/allergen information verified from that recipe. Do not infer that every version of a dish has the same ingredients.

No complete recipe has yet been established in this KB.

# Odisha’s poda and fire-cooking traditions

**Odisha’s Best-Kept Secret — The Art of Cooking with Fire** is the user-selected campaign wording. The evidence supports a varied poda repertoire; it does not establish an official title, national ranking, exclusive origin or one cooking technique. “Best-kept secret” is a creative tag, not a measured awareness finding.

## A menu connected by heat

This selection brings together nine food identities, not a statewide count. Ingredients cross vegetables, mushrooms, fish, prawns, chicken, meat, rice and cheese. Evidence ranges from contributors’ recipes to institutional descriptions and historical menu specifications.

| Food | Method in the cited account | Source scope |
|---|---|---|
| [Baigana poda](baigana-poda.md) | direct roasting | Contributor recipe; pakhala accompaniment. |
| [Tomato / bilati baigana poda](tomato-poda.md) | direct roasting | Contributor recipe; no district attribution. |
| [Chatu patrapoda](chatu-patrapoda.md) | leaf parcel | Contributor home version; distinct from the saved 2019 restaurant account. |
| [Machha patrapoda](machha-patrapoda.md) | leaf parcel | Contributor home version; not evidence of a unique Odisha invention. |
| [Chingudi patrapoda](chingudi-patrapoda.md) | leaf parcel | Historical restaurant interpretation reported by Mansita Mishra. |
| [Kukuda patrapoda](kukuda-patrapoda.md) | leaf parcel | Proposed/specification menu, not proof of current restaurant availability. |
| [Baunsa poda mansa](baunsa-poda-mansa.md) | bamboo cooking | Attributed reporting; detailed Araku recipe is not transferred to Odisha. |
| [Poda pitha](poda-pitha.md) | slow baking | Reuse of saved attributed regional accounts; versions are not universal rules. |
| [Chhena poda](chhena-poda.md) | slow baking | Reuse of institutional overview; modern oven versions need no direct flame. |

## What the connection means

Direct roasting exposes vegetables to heat before peeling/mashing. Leaf parcels enclose food and can combine surface charring with moisture retained inside. Bamboo is a cooking vessel in the meat account. Baking gives rice cakes and cheese sweets another route to a browned surface. These are related for this editorial collection; they are not interchangeable definitions of barbecue.

[Pakhala](pakhala.md) supplies an everyday meal connection through Sasmita’s baigana recipe. [Poda pitha](poda-pitha.md) supplies festival context through the saved Raja account. [Chhena poda](chhena-poda.md) lets the story finish with a sweet. This is an editorial tasting sequence, not a documented traditional set meal or bookable tour.

[Enduri pitha](enduri-pitha.md) is a useful boundary: it is leaf-wrapped and steamed. Leaves alone do not make a dish barbecue. Lopa’s account also describes a modern enclosed daba-poda adaptation; the name alone does not prove charring. The food traditions shared with neighbouring regions must retain their own credits; resemblance does not establish migration or historical influence.

## Evidence limits and next work

- Obtain named Odisha community and cook accounts for bamboo-cooked meat and chicken parcels; broad “tribal” attribution is insufficient for an origin claim.
- Deepen sukhua poda, alu poda, bhendi/janhi/potala poda and leaf choice only after source verification. These are leads, not confirmed additions to the nine-entry selection.
- Keep the Nimantran procurement menu separate from operating/serving evidence. Its steamed chhena-poda description conflicts with the baking account, and is held unresolved.
- The CCRT-hosted folklore PDF failed direct retrieval and a 50-second network retry. Indexed bamboo references are discovery leads only; retry 8 October 2026 if needed.
- Recipe quantities, smoke chemistry, nutritional benefits, origin dates, comparative state rankings and economic impact are not established here. No new revenue, export or popularity numbers.

[Structured evidence](../references/data/poda-traditions.json) · [Story and video draft](../stories/odisha-poda-country.md) · [Preparation collection](preparation-and-variation.md).

body:
# How Odisha cooks: preparations and variations

Fourteen entries now connect names to preparation accounts: six pitha, four everyday dishes and four place-linked sweets. These are the bounds of this research batch, not a count of Odisha’s foods. Explore the linked entries for ingredients, sources and differences; their versions are attributed rather than prescribed as one authentic recipe.

## Pitha: follow the cooking method

- [Chakuli pitha](chakuli.md) — pan cooking, fermentation.
- [Poda pitha](poda-pitha.md) — slow cooking, leaf assisted cooking.
- [Enduri pitha](enduri-pitha.md) — steaming, leaf wrapping.
- [Sijha manda pitha](manda-pitha.md) — boiling, steaming, filled dumpling.
- [Kakara pitha](kakara-pitha.md) — frying, filled dough.
- [Arisa pitha](arisa-pitha.md) — frying.

## Everyday dishes and sweets

- [Pakhala](pakhala.md) — soaking, fermentation.
- [Dalma](dalma.md) — boiling, tempering.
- [Chatu patrapoda](chatu-patrapoda.md) — leaf wrapping, fire cooking.
- [Ou khatta](ou-khatta.md) — boiling, tempering and simmering.
- [Chhena poda](chhena-poda.md) — baking, leaf assisted cooking.
- [Chhena jhili](chhena-jhili.md) — frying, syrup soaking.
- [Kendrapara Rasabali](kendrapara-rasabali.md) — frying, milk soaking.
- [Dhenkanal Magji](dhenkanal-magji.md) — pressing, pan cooking, hand shaping.

## What still needs a cook’s voice

Regional distribution, household measurements, preferred Odia names and demonstrated variations remain open. A contributor recipe hosted by a government portal retains its author’s scope. A restaurant interpretation does not establish temple practice. No field interview, recipe test or human language review has been invented.

Magji’s original specification is now available, but its internal sugar proportions differ. Enduri’s new steaming detail remains indexed-only because the hospitality PDF could not be retrieved. The collection retains those limits rather than silently turning them into recipe instructions.

[Structured preparation register](../references/data/food-preparations.json) keeps each account, locator, scope and unresolved question together. [Rasagola and sweets economics](../economy/rasagola-and-sweets.md) owns the separate sales/export questions. No commercial totals, health claims or serving venues were added here.

## Follow-up: original records and regional voices · 1 October 2026

Seven of the existing entries now have additional evidence. The [2015 rice-food book](../sources/food-crri-rice2015.md) supplies full preparation passages for six pitha, including Enduri; its new capture resolves the earlier reliance on an indexed-only steaming description without claiming that the unavailable NCHM PDF was recovered. [Poda pitha](poda-pitha.md) now separates named book versions and attributed coastal/western accounts.

[Rasabali](kendrapara-rasabali.md) now preserves both the original GI specification and September correction. Conflicting curdling instructions remain visible. Undated seller/maker claims are held as economics leads, with no sales or exports inferred. Earlier checkpoints above describe the evidence available at that time.

Next: independent local preparations for chatu patrapoda and ou khatta; finer regional attribution where supported. Recipe testing and local/Odia review remain pending.

## Poda story extension · 1 October 2026

[Poda and fire cooking](poda-and-fire-cooking.md) connects existing pitha, cheese and mushroom entries with six new scoped food nuclei. Chatu now has Lopa’s own home preparation alongside the chef-menu account; locality review remains open. Ou khatta remains the next distinct preparation gap.

## Fourteen-food research set complete · 1 October 2026

[Ou khatta](ou-khatta.md) now distinguishes two preparations by Sasmita and a family meal memory by Julie Acharya Ray. This closes the last attributed-preparation gap in the bounded RES-011 set of six pitha, four everyday dishes and four place-linked sweets. It does not complete statewide coverage, recipe testing, local language review or the resolution of every source conflict. Further poda and locality questions remain in the existing records. Next sequential task: sweets economics (RES-031).

# Odisha garments, cloth and markets

A garment is what someone wears; fibre, weaving technique, named tradition and production place describe different aspects of it. Keep these separate so that a Sambalpuri saree, a shirt made from Bandha fabric and factory-produced apparel are not counted as the same product.

Boyanika’s checked navigation offers research leads for **sarees, three-piece dress materials, kurtis, waistcoats, kurtas, shirts, jackets, dupattas/scarves, shawls and stoles**. Running fabric, home textiles and accessories are additional categories. Navigation establishes advertised categories, not stock, garment origin or export shipments.

## Tradition and cultural context

| Existing tradition | Saved place or process evidence | Detail to deepen |
|---|---|---|
| [Sambalpuri Bandha](sambalpuri-bandha.md) | Western Odisha; historical GI record | Tie-dye process, motifs, named makers and garment forms |
| [Bomkai](bomkai.md) | Silk production in Sonepur/Boudh | Distinguish origin village from present production centres |
| [Khandua](khandua.md) | Nuapatna silk and calligraphy textiles | Text, ritual use and attribution of each piece |
| [Kotpad](kotpad.md) | Mirgan weavers and aul-root dye reference | Maker-reviewed community names, dye process and use |
| [Habaspuri](habaspuri.md) | Kalahandi | Technique and current continuity |
| [Berhampuri Patta](berhampuri-patta.md) | Southern Odisha silk tradition | Construction, ceremonial use and maker provenance |
| [Tussar centres](tussar-centres.md) | Several named weaving centres | Fibre, provenance and disambiguated place names |

These rows reuse saved source checks. They are not a fresh verification of each tradition or a claim that each is exported.

## Market evidence

The [export series](../statistics/textile-and-apparel-exports.md) covers textiles, apparel and handicrafts together. The [2019–20 workforce census](../statistics/craft-livelihoods.md) records weavers and allied workers separately. Neither assigns export income to a named weaving tradition.

The OGD segment-wise resource identifies a parliamentary source, but its rows did not render. Its 2024–25 column covers **April–September 2024 only**. Retrieve the original table before comparing categories. Seek verified Odisha factory production, shipment origin, destination, HS code, quantity, value and year; company-wide garment output cannot be relabelled as Odisha output.

[Structured product and evidence register](../references/data/creative-economy.json).

[Textile export evidence](../statistics/textile-and-apparel-exports.md) — Read garment traditions beside broad sector exports without assigning the aggregate to any named weave.

# Bali and Indonesia: three distinct kinds of connection

Ardika and Bellwood’s Sembiran research identifies early Indian contact with Bali.[^maritime-sembiran] Odisha’s official Bali Jatra account commemorates maritime exchange with Southeast Asia, particularly Bali.[^maritime-culture-2025]

## Link carefully

The first supports an archaeological India–Bali connection; the second establishes a contemporary Odisha commemoration. Neither alone proves that every Indian object in Bali came from modern Odisha. The research graph keeps both links without collapsing them into an exclusive origin claim.

## An epigraphic lead

A scholarly discussion references foreign communities including Kling in Javanese inscriptions. This edition records it as a lead: the underlying transcription, dating and geographic interpretation must be checked. The term must not be automatically equated with modern Odia identity.[^maritime-cane-lead]

## Commercial next step

Obtain Odisha-origin exports to Indonesia by product and year, then identify an actual buyer or producer relationship. National India–Indonesia totals cannot fill a state-level data gap.

[Boita Bandana](../culture/boita-bandana.md) · [Country connection matrix](../trade/connection-matrix.md)

# Buddhist learning in Odisha: Pushpagiri and the monastic landscape

**Pushpagiri is a promising research focus for the ancient learning question.** The [Jajpur exhibition](https://artsandculture.google.com/story/the-buddhist-heritage-of-jajpur-jajpur/NwWh9wDVsCTFtg?hl=en), whose story is credited to Live History India, identifies Langudi with Pushpagiri and connects it to Xuanzang’s account. This is a curated interpretation, not our own reading of an inscription or excavation report.

We already maintain [Ratnagiri](../places/ratnagiri.md), [Lalitgiri](../places/lalitgiri.md) and [Udayagiri](../places/udayagiri-buddhist.md). Keep them as distinct archaeological identities. A modern circuit name does not prove they formed one university.

The next batch must examine excavation publications, inscriptions and the relevant translated traveller passage, with dates, pages and competing identifications. Use *monastery* or *mahavihara* where the evidence supports it; a modern university analogy needs explanation. No enrolment figure, institutional continuity, Asian rank or “most significant university” claim is established.

A broader Buddhist history should distinguish Ashokan inscriptions and the Kalinga-war account, later monastic phases, Buddhist philosophical traditions, objects and manuscripts, and living communities. Links to Southeast Asia require evidence for each person, object or text, rather than an assumed universal influence.

# Forest livelihoods: a documented history

**Use dated evidence to explain how collection, household knowledge and trading institutions changed.** A publication date is not the beginning of a tradition.

- **1973:** OFDC's institutional history places kendu nationalisation in this year. Its page also describes later deregulation in named areas. This is a historical anchor, not a statement of today's collection permissions. [OFDC](https://www.odishafdc.com/kenduleaf.php).
- **2001:** Nanda and Sutar's Vasundhara study, hosted by FAO, connects mahua and kendu livelihoods with community forest management and fire. Its cases need local attribution; the title/abstract district mismatch remains unresolved. This does not establish one uniform tribal practice. [Original study](https://www.fao.org/4/ad352t/AD352T06.htm).
- **2018 publication:** Mishra and Pradhan examine household use and marketing channels in a six-village Kendujhar sample. Fieldwork dates and full methods still require the original text. [Study record](https://ideas.repec.org/a/ags/injagm/399613.html).

## Extend the timeline carefully

Research precolonial exchange only where dated documentary or archaeological evidence supports it; then examine colonial forest administration, cooperatives, changes in collector rights, women's enterprise and contemporary processing. Retain oral histories as attributed accounts with consent and provenance; no interviews have been conducted for this entry. Study food preservation, seasonal labour and changing household uses alongside laws and commercial institutions.

[Forest foods](../food/forest-foods.md) · [Markets and livelihoods](../economy/forest-products.md).

# A stone anchor connects Odisha and Gujarat

Tripati and colleagues analysed a broken medieval-type anchor found at Manikapatna using petrography, chemistry and isotopes. They identified Palitana-area Deccan basalt in Gujarat as its most likely rock source.[^maritime-anchor]

## Why it matters

This is a material-provenance connection, stronger than a resemblance-based cultural claim. It supports investigating movement across the Indian coastal network. The finding does not identify a ship, crew, itinerary or traded cargo quantity.

## Marketing treatment

“A stone with a journey to tell.” Show the object only with correct attribution and image rights; animate the relationship as probable provenance, not a reconstructed sailing track.

# Manikapatna: overseas objects and a port site

The 2026 research abstract reports Chinese ceramics and Chinese and Sri Lankan coins at Manikapatna; it describes activity around the sixth–seventh through seventeenth centuries CE.[^maritime-manikapatna-2026]

The 2022 paper reports earlier excavation phases of second century BCE–fifth/sixth century CE and ninth–nineteenth century CE.[^maritime-anchor]

title: Maritime Odisha: the evidence structure
description: Maritime Odisha: the evidence structure — evidence, scope and reuse.
body:
# Maritime Odisha: the evidence structure

Odisha’s maritime story can be connected through objects, sites, commemorations and modern trade observations. Those links support an outward-looking commercial identity. They do not supply an ancient export ledger or a continuous company history.

## The strongest connected stories

| Connection | Historical or cultural anchor | Modern link | Claim boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| China | [Ceramic and coin finds](manikapatna.md), plus [Khalkatapatna](khalkatapatna.md) | [Export destination observation](../trade/export-destinations.md) | Archaeological circulation does not specify a direct sailing route |
| Sri Lanka | Reported coins at [Manikapatna](manikapatna.md) | Odisha-specific current trade value still needed | No invented modern total |
| Indonesia / Bali | [Commemoration](../culture/boita-bandana.md) and [India–Bali archaeological research](bali-and-indonesia.md) | Country-specific state export and buyer data still needed | Indian contact is not automatically Odisha-exclusive |
| Malay Peninsula | [Published route reconstruction](palur-and-bay-routes.md) | Malaysia appears in the export-destination table | Historical region and modern national territory are different |
| Gujarat | [Archaeometric provenance of an anchor](manikapatna-anchor.md) | Potential contemporary coastal-logistics research | Rock provenance is not a complete ship itinerary |
| Enterprise in Odisha | [Boita Bandana](../culture/boita-bandana.md) | [Paradip’s own commemoration](../trade/paradip-bridge.md) and [fair sales reporting](../trade/baliyatra-commerce.md) | Cultural pride is not a measured cause of business performance |

## A chronology with visible uncertainty

Read each site’s dated record separately. The 2022 Manikapatna paper’s archaeological phases and the 2026 conference abstract’s activity window are not identical. Neither should be converted into “uninterrupted global trade for 2,000 years.” Object dates, occupation dates and voyage dates are different variables.

## Geographic discipline

Use Utkal · Odisha as the campaign identity. In historical records, retain the source’s Kalinga, Utkal or Odra terminology and time-dependent geography. Do not assign every port of the wider historical east-coast network to today’s Odisha. Treat cultural transmission as a specific, testable proposition: which practice or object, at which place and date, with what evidence of direction?

## Reusable data

The [linked-data method](../methods/maritime-linked-data.md) explains the entity and claim graph. A missing number is stored as missing, never as zero. The [research queue](research-agenda.md) prioritises the remaining trade and historical joins.

## Evidence type

Ports named together in a network may lie in different present-day states. A network link can be commercially meaningful without being exclusive to one region.

title: Next evidence needed for a global trading story
description: Next evidence needed for a global trading story — evidence, scope and reuse.
body:
# Next evidence needed for a global trading story

## Highest-value joins

1. **Odisha → country → product → year:** obtain official state-of-origin exports at HS product-code level, in both value and quantity, for China, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and Sri Lanka. Retain state-of-origin methodology, revisions, currencies and complete annual series. This will identify real product relationships rather than relying on country-level symbolism.
2. **Product → producer → buyer:** identify public, attributable commercial examples in metals, seafood, textiles and food. Confirm actual shipments or contracts before treating plans or trade-fair meetings as outcomes.
3. **Festival → seller → sales:** obtain ORMAS and district closing reports, definitions of sales, participating-stall counts and event dates. Separate visitor entries from unique people; avoid economic-impact multipliers without a study.
4. **Object → excavation → origin:** retrieve Manikapatna and Khalkatapatna catalogues, accession identifiers, dating methods and museum locations. Ask a qualified archaeologist to review the proposed public claims.
5. **Inscription → transcription → translation:** pursue the Kling/Cane and related Javanese leads through original editions and current scholarship. Historical ethnonyms need contextual interpretation.
6. **Cultural influence:** investigate one named practice or object at a time with Indonesian and other regional scholarship. Similarity alone does not establish source, direction or exclusive authorship.

## Known issues to preserve

- Manikapatna chronology differs across the 2022 research paper and 2026 abstract.
- The 2019 Roman-contact paper’s discussion is substantially more cautious than its abstract.
- Export destination percentages need underlying-table denominator reconciliation before conversion into rupee values.
- The survey’s marine-destination Figure 4.9 contains an unresolved editorial note about quantity versus value; do not substitute those shares for the overall export-destination table.
- The 2024 fair-sales article has inconsistent title metadata and lacks an audited closing statement.

## Measurement plan

For future campaigns, track qualified enquiries, maker referrals, completed purchases, export leads progressing to confirmed orders and visitor bookings with consented attribution. Set a baseline before launch. Historical content is an entry point; business outcomes need contemporary measurement.

This is a research queue, not evidence that ancient trade volumes, trader counts or market shares are known. The initial maritime module is not an exhaustive archive of all Odisha history.

# Roman connections: why the full paper changes the claim

The 2019 reassessment questions several supposed Roman finds and concludes that direct Odisha–Roman maritime contact lacks tangible support in the evidence reviewed. Indirect exchange remains a possibility.[^maritime-romans-2019]

## Research consequence

Its abstract can sound stronger than its conclusion. Read the discussion on pages 1394–1395 before citing the paper. Do not use “Odisha traded directly with Rome” as an established headline on the basis of this source.

This does not negate Odisha’s wider maritime history. It identifies which particular route claim is unresolved. Keep this record discoverable so future marketing research does not repeatedly pick up the stronger, unsupported version.

## Geographic naming

The paper also distinguishes historical names and changing boundaries. That supports retaining historical geography separately from present-day state identity.

# Scientific knowledge preserved in manuscripts

Odisha’s manuscript heritage gives the science timeline a second route: follow surviving catalogue records alongside biographies. The museum’s undated department page describes approximately 37,000 manuscripts across 27 categories, including mathematics, astronomy/astrology and medicine. Its separate collection table gives 37,273. Neither is a current science-manuscript count or a measure of unique works. The pages provide no common inventory date, so no change is calculated. [Department](https://odishamuseum.nic.in/?q=dept/manuscripts); [collection table](https://www.odishamuseum.nic.in/?q=node/5).

## Bhāsvatī beyond Odisha

IGNCA’s 2024 catalogue, printed p.102, records *Bhāsvatī* witnesses at BORI in Pune, Kamarupa Anusandhan Samiti in Guwahati and Saraswati Bhawan Library in Varanasi. Four selected entries retain catalogue identifiers, folio counts, completeness and scripts in the [evidence register](../references/data/science-heritage.json). The Guwahati entry credits a commentary to Karirāja Cakravarti. These are catalogue descriptions of manuscripts represented in IGNCA’s microfilm collection, not four independent historical studies. [Catalogue](https://ignca.gov.in/PDF_data/Jyotish-Vol-6-Part-1.pdf#page=120).

This extends the [Bhāsvatī work record](../works/bhasvati.md) with institutional catalogue evidence. Repository locations demonstrate documented preservation beyond Odisha; they do not establish when the text travelled, its influence abroad or a continuous scientific institution. The work’s composition date and a surviving copy’s date are different fields. Unspecified Saṁvat dates remain unconverted.

## Mathematics on palm leaf

The museum’s [Ganita catalogue](https://odishamuseum.nic.in/?field_abstraction_tid=All&field_author_value=&field_category_tid=All&field_subject_value=&page=1&q=palm-leaf-g) lists *Lilabati Pati Ganita* (G/141), *Ganita Chautisha* (G/43) and *Khadi Pothi* (G/112) as palm-leaf records. Their displayed author fields are blank. Names, dates, language interpretation and intellectual content need manuscript-level checks before these can become credited scientist profiles. A title containing a poetic form offers a research lead for science and literary expression, not proof of a particular teaching practice.

## What remains open

INSA’s bibliography confirms Deepak Bhattacharya’s eight-page 2008 survey in *Indian Journal of History of Science* 43(1), pp.101–108. The full survey could not be retrieved; its table entries remain unverified leads. [Publisher index](https://insaindia.res.in/history-of-science/).

The Devīdāsa commentary lead in the already saved Panda study still needs an identifiable manuscript record. No new early scientist has been inferred from surname, text title or custody alone. Original folios, colophons, acquisition histories and specialist attribution remain the next evidence layer. Museum scanning and online catalogue presence do not establish complete digitisation, public full-text access or reuse rights.

[Scientific heritage timeline](../people/science-and-contributions.md) — Read manuscript records alongside named contributors; collection custody does not establish an author’s Odisha origin.

# Odisha FDI index — recorded inflows and trends

**Current use:** Background reference. The user replaced the standalone FDI focus with [Investment in Odisha](investment.md). The weekly agent no longer monitors this as an independent headline track. The saved numbers were rechecked against DPIIT Table 5 on 27 September 2026; the USD-million units are confirmed.

## The reader’s takeaway

**US$69.72 million of FDI equity inflows recorded in 2025.**

The comparable calendar-year figures were **US$11.83 million in 2023** and **US$4.41 million in 2024**. The 2025 rise was **US$65.31 million**, or approximately **15.8 times** the 2024 amount, from a small base.[^journey-fdi-mar2026]

## Index scope

This is an organised tracker of official **FDI equity inflows**, not a new composite investment-attractiveness score. DPIIT’s state detail covers the equity component; it is not total FDI including reinvested earnings and other capital.[^journey-fdi-mar2026]

## The saved time windows

- **2023:** US$11.83 million.
- **2024:** US$4.41 million.
- **2025:** US$69.72 million.
- **January–March 2026:** US$14.68 million; a partial year.
- **October 2019–March 2026:** reported cumulative US$257.19 million, also reported as ₹2,054.88 crore.[^journey-fdi-mar2026]

All figures above are recorded as assigned to Odisha in the cited DPIIT table. The three full-year observations are calendar years. The table pools October 2019–December 2022 into one US$156.54-million cell; that cell is not an annual observation.

## Meaning and presentation

Show the three complete years as directly labelled bars beginning at zero. Put the 2026 partial-year value on a separate card. Prefer “FDI equity inflows rebounded in 2025” with the absolute values visible. A 15.8× headline alone would overstate the breadth of evidence by concealing the small base.

Use the source’s reported INR and USD values; do not treat their ratio as a current exchange rate. Keep investment summits, domestic project proposals, approved project costs and announced foreign interest in a separate pipeline collection.

## Calculation and scope notes

The year-on-year percentage change is derived from the displayed rounded source inputs. The table’s rounded component periods sum to US$257.18 million, while it reports US$257.19 million cumulatively. Retain the reported cumulative figure and the US$0.01-million rounding difference. The underlying unrounded observations are unavailable here.

No five- or ten-year growth rate, comprehensive state ranking or sector/investor attribution is established by this short series. The source ends in March 2026; this record does not claim it is the latest release available in September 2026. A newer-release check is part of the research queue.
