## Reconciliation checkpoint · 30 September 2026

The Ministry's [8 December 2025 release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2200323&lang=1&reg=6), Annexure I, reports **87,854 foreign tourist visits in 2024** and **45,173 in 2023** for Odisha. The higher 2024 count therefore appears in an earlier central release as well as the saved February 2026 table. This is corroboration within government reporting, not an independent enumeration.

The state bulletin's saved **53,392** remains unresolved. No correction or definition bridge was found. Keep foreign-growth and affected total-visit headlines on hold. The ministry explicitly separates state visits from international arrivals; neither is a count of unique travellers to Odisha. Follow the annexure's 2020–2024 columns despite a wider period mentioned in surrounding prose.

[Reconciliation evidence](../references/data/tourism-series-reconciliation.json) preserves the checks and failures. [Tourism comparison](../economy/comparison-09-tourism.md) shows why a conflicting component also affects the total; [source recovery](../methods/source-reliability.md) records the remaining document work.

## Community-managed programme evidence

[Ecotourism](ecotourism.md) now has a dated primary income/visitor series. Its narrower programme scope must not be added to statewide tourist-visit totals.

# Editorial journey: Odisha’s Buddhist circuit

**Proposed opening:** “Let the stone tell the story.”

Commission an archaeologist or qualified guide to explain one object, structure or discovery at each site. A visual sequence can move from a close detail to the wider site and then its historical context. Religious significance should be explained with care and attribution.

Before publishing a trip, verify the current museum and site arrangements, transport, guiding availability and interpretation. Do not conflate Jajpur’s Buddhist Udayagiri with the Jain caves near Bhubaneswar. Relic identifications require attributed language rather than certainty added for dramatic effect.

Potential audiences include heritage travellers, students and visitors interested in Buddhist history. Market demand has not yet been measured.

# Growing Odisha: numbers with a human setting

**Campaign line:** “See what is taking shape.”

The [GDP story](../economy/gdp-story.md) introduces scale. Individual features can then explain a port, an industrial activity, fisheries or a service business through an attributed participant and a relevant measure.

Suggested first stories:

- [Fish production](../economy/comparison-01-fisheries.md): a ten-year physical-output comparison, paired with a producer-led account. Do not convert production growth into an unmeasured income claim.
- [Paradip throughput](../economy/comparison-05-port-logistics.md): a port logistics story with the period clearly visible. Do not infer the same growth for all Odisha trade.
- [Construction real value added](../economy/construction.md): a five-year sector chart, with local examples researched separately. Do not present all output as government infrastructure.

Use one measure per poster, the full period beside it and a legible source note. A short video can put the number on screen once and spend its remaining time explaining the activity behind it.

Proposed investment records should form a separate “what is planned” sequence. An approved project, a groundbreaking and commercial production are different milestones.

body:
# Odisha’s Best-Kept Secret — The Art of Cooking with Fire — campaign draft

## Campaign direction

**Odisha’s Best-Kept Secret**

*The Art of Cooking with Fire*

The user selected this campaign tag and subtitle on 1 October 2026. “Best-kept secret” is evocative editorial language, not a measured claim about awareness. Introduce poda within the story and explain the different cooking methods. Campaign wording approval does not establish factual review, media rights or website publication approval.

## Reader-facing story draft

Start with a vegetable, and follow the heat. Baigana poda turns roasted eggplant into a mustard-scented mash; tomato poda brings another roasted accompaniment to the table. Move to the parcels: mushrooms and fish seasoned and folded into leaves, or prawns charred inside sal leaves. Each wrapper makes the opening part of the meal. [Vegetable account](../food/baigana-poda.md), [tomato account](../food/tomato-poda.md), [mushroom and fish](../sources/food-patrapoda-lopa2024.md), [prawns](../food/chingudi-patrapoda.md).

Then widen the story. A historical Odisha Tourism menu describes leaf-cooked chicken; published reporting connects Odisha’s baunsa poda mansa with meat cooked inside bamboo. These are invitations to meet and credit the cooks behind each preparation, with local details still to document. [Chicken evidence](../food/kukuda-patrapoda.md), [bamboo evidence](../food/baunsa-poda-mansa.md).

The finish can be sweet. Poda pitha brings rice and festival memories; chhena poda brings fresh cheese and a browned surface. Roasted, wrapped or baked, the connection runs across ingredients and courses. **Discover the many ways Odisha cooks.** [Pitha](../food/poda-pitha.md), [cheese sweet](../food/chhena-poda.md).

## Short video script · draft

Estimated 35–45 seconds; not recorded or timed with the user’s clone.

“In Odisha, follow one word: poda. Start with roasted eggplant. Add tomato, sharp with mustard oil. Open a leaf parcel: mushrooms, fish or prawns. Follow the story to chicken in leaves and meat cooked inside bamboo. Then stay for dessert: poda pitha and chhena poda. Roasting, leaf cooking, slow baking—different methods, a delicious connection. Odisha’s best-kept secret: the art of cooking with fire.”

Visual sequence proposal: vegetable roasting → opening a leaf parcel → a credited bamboo-cooking demonstration → slicing pitha and chhena poda. Use consented, correctly labelled footage of the actual method. An oven-baked example must not be presented as a filmed ember preparation. Media and music rights remain unestablished; no video has been generated.

## Poster copy · draft

ODISHA’S BEST-KEPT SECRET

The Art of Cooking with Fire

From roasted vegetables and leaf-wrapped delicacies to caramelised sweets—discover Odisha’s poda traditions.

## Editorial evidence controls

The [nine-entry evidence collection](../food/poda-and-fire-cooking.md) distinguishes source types, methods and unresolved fields. The linked draft is a proposed tasting narrative, not a traditional fixed menu or an available tour. Do not claim “everything is barbecued”, oldest/largest/best in India, uniquely Odishan leaf cooking, or a common origin for all these foods. Enduri’s steaming and modern enclosed/oven adaptations stay distinct. No recipe testing, human factual review, measured audience response or publication approval is claimed.

# Taste Odisha: a collection of kitchens

**Campaign line:** “One state. So many ways to welcome you.”

Open with the act of serving. Move between [pakhala](../food/pakhala.md), [dalma](../food/dalma.md), the [pitha collection](../food/pitha.md) and a [chhena poda](../food/chhena-poda.md) slice. Let each contributor explain what the food means in their own home or business. These selected examples introduce a collection; they do not stand in for every community’s cuisine.

## Proposed formats

- Poster: one dish, its name, place or contributor, and one sensory line grounded in the photographed preparation.
- Short feature: one maker, one attributed preparation, one variation and one occasion.
- Video: serving close-up, maker’s voice, process detail, finished plate and place name.

For a national audience, test “your next food journey.” For international audiences, retain the local name and add a plain-language ingredient or technique description. Gather audience response before choosing a universal message.

## Production needs

Recipe confirmation, contributor consent, original imagery, correct names, ingredient-specific allergy information and current visitor details where a business is featured. The user’s AI clone can provide a connecting introduction once the chosen service and asset are available; the KB does not contain a rendered clone video.

body:
# Utkal: a trading culture, building its next global chapter

## Positioning

**Utkal · Odisha**

**A trading culture. A new global chapter.**

The commercial proposition is that Odisha already has modern trade activity worth showing, and a distinctive way to introduce it. Heritage supplies the opening; present evidence supplies the business case.

## Story sequence

Open with [Boita Bandana](../culture/boita-bandana.md), then show the [Paradip institutional connection](../trade/paradip-bridge.md). Move to the port’s measured activity and the state’s merchandise-export comparison. End with a named maker or business, researched separately, and a useful next action.

The question “If we could do it then, why can’t we do it now?” becomes: **“We are trading today. What can we build next?”** This invites ambition without pretending that an ancient achievement forecasts modern performance.

## Three campaign directions

- **Trade has a place in our culture.** A ritual-led film connected to an actual institution and its work.
- **Odisha is already connected.** A contemporary trade feature with destinations, products and counterparties as the evidence grows.
- **The next voyage begins with what we make.** A maker or exporter portrait leading to an attributable purchase or business enquiry.

## Copy ready for development

“Every voyage begins with the courage to look beyond the shore. In Odisha, the memory of the maritime trader is still celebrated. Today, a new chapter is being written by the people who make, move and trade. Meet the Odisha building its place in the world.”

This is campaign copy. Support accompanying factual captions through the [headline bank](../trade/headline-bank.md). The line does not assert that every modern enterprise descends from ancient traders.

## Creative treatment

Use the project’s deep red, ivory and ochre palette. Pair miniature boats with contemporary activity through an editorial transition, not a simulated historical reconstruction presented as documentary footage. Mark illustrative animation as illustration. Include local voices and credited work.

## Claim discipline

Choose strong facts and clear comparisons. Do not knowingly create a false impression by dropping the unit, hiding a crucial denominator, converting an interpretation into certainty, or making a proposed project look operational. That preserves the campaign’s ability to stand up to scrutiny.

# Woven in Odisha: meet the making

**Campaign line:** “Know the hands. Know the cloth.”

Begin with a single piece rather than a sweeping claim. A [Kotpad](../handlooms/kotpad.md) textile, a [Khandua](../handlooms/khandua.md) piece or a [Habaspuri](../handlooms/habaspuri.md) example can each lead to a distinct portrait. Ask the maker to explain the decisions visible in the finished cloth.

## Proposed feature structure

Show the whole piece, then a detail. Name the maker and making place. Explain the technique only after it has been verified for that piece. Include material, care and a transparent purchase route where one is established. Record the source of all sustainability claims separately.

For fashion audiences, style a credited object in contemporary use. For design audiences, document process and material choices. Do not describe every Odisha textile as Sambalpuri or every patterned textile as ikat.

## Commercial research

Interview participating makers about commissions, capacity, payment terms and how they want to be represented. Check a seller’s product provenance and current fulfilment. A story should help readers understand value without inventing income, labour-time or market-demand statistics.

# Economy, livelihoods and infrastructure

Examine how Odisha produces, works, finances enterprise and connects with markets. Separate output from income, credit balances from investment, and approvals from operating capacity. Transport and digital networks belong here as infrastructure and also connect to daily life.

## Homestays and local enterprise

## Evidence to explore

**MSME advances outstanding: 120,396.58 INR crore** — 2026-06-30; Odisha.[^macro-slbc-jun2026]

Reported balance at date, not lending disbursed during the year. Sector balances overlap; do not sum into investment. State utilised-credit scope differs from in-state sanction scope.

**Internet subscriptions: 30.56 million subscriptions** — 2026-03-31; Odisha.[^weekly-trai-mar2026]

All Odisha state-based internet subscriptions, broadband plus narrowband, wired plus wireless; density uses projected population. Subscriptions are not unique users; density may exceed 100. Rounded components sum to 30.55 million versus reported 30.56. Prior March 2025 source carried some operator data forward; no unqualified growth comparison made.


## Connections worth following

- [How much money is held in banks and how much credit remains outstanding?](../statistics/banking-and-credit.md) Bank balances and women’s use of accounts answer different questions about finance.
- [Which enterprises are recognised under each programme?](../statistics/startups.md) Recognition and scheme finance use different populations.
- [How much cargo moves through the port?](../statistics/ports.md) Cargo tonnage and export value describe different flows.
- [How is connectivity measured?](../statistics/digital-connectivity.md) Compare subscription counts with survey-reported use, without equating accounts and people.

## Local case study

[Debrigarh: community livelihoods and nature](../places/debrigarh-hirakud.md) connects a dated reported engagement figure to place, people and conservation questions. Employment, income and ecological outcomes remain separate measures.

## Gaps to deepen

Project-level realised spending, firm survival, jobs and wages, logistics outcomes and comparable long-run series.

title: Technical architecture diagrams

instruction_basis: User-agreed launch architecture in the Odisha Tourism conversation, 27 September 2026. Future stages are proposals; no deployment or billing change is implied.
body:
# Technical architecture diagrams

## How to read these diagrams

The launch diagram records the agreed design, not an already running system. The growth diagram records optional future capabilities. Solid paths represent intended flows, not integrations that have been tested. Private submissions pass through editorial review before any public Git change.

## Launch architecture

![Launch architecture: maintainers publish reviewed OKF content through Astro and GitHub Pages; visitors contribute through private email or Firebase Spark.](../references/diagrams/launch-architecture.svg)

[Editable SVG](../references/diagrams/launch-architecture.svg) · [Mermaid source](../references/diagrams/launch-architecture.mmd)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  M[Maintainers and reviewers] -->|Reviewed public changes| G[Canonical OKF and approved photos in Git]
  G --> B[Validation and Astro build]
  B --> P[GitHub Pages: pages, data and Pagefind]
  P --> V[Visitors on our domain]
  V -->|Photo form or email| R[Free relay candidate or direct email]
  R --> I[Private editorial inbox]
  I -->|Rights, evidence and credit review| M
  V --> A[Firebase Authentication: Spark]
  V -->|Rule-authorised text and user data| F[Firestore: Spark]
  F -->|Manual editorial review| M
```

Authentication supplies identity to Firestore rules; an arrow to Firestore does not imply public database access. Privileged roles are assigned by maintainers. The inbox contains photo attachments; Firestore does not automatically mirror it. Public pages and search do not depend on live Firestore reads.

GA4 is omitted from the drawing for clarity. It receives only approved public events after consent; it is not a content store or a copy of the private queue. Public DNS points to GitHub Pages. Assets and API requests remain separate.

## Future architecture

![Growth architecture: keep Git and the approved public release, adding managed uploads, review automation, cited AI or private recovery only as needed.](../references/diagrams/growth-architecture.svg)

[Editable SVG](../references/diagrams/growth-architecture.svg) · [Mermaid source](../references/diagrams/growth-architecture.mmd)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  G[Git and OKF remain canonical] --> B[Approved versioned release]
  B --> W[Public website and data]
  U[Future private managed uploads] --> R[Future review service]
  R -->|Proposed Git change, then editorial approval| G
  B --> K[Future public-only AI retrieval index]
  K --> Q[Future Ask Utkal gateway]
  Q -->|Cited answer| W
  U --> C[Future private backup and restore]
  R --> C
```

Future services must not become an independent master encyclopedia. Private uploads, consent and account data remain excluded from public exports and AI retrieval. A paid plan, a free model tier or a proposed diagram does not by itself establish service availability, accuracy or recovery.

## Three operational sequences

1. **Read:** load a static page and its versioned data/search assets. User-specific features request only authorised private records.
2. **Contribute:** a photo arrives through the activated relay or email; a text proposal arrives in Firestore. An editor reviews it, then creates a public Git change. Only its approved content and credited media are published.
3. **Correct:** update the source concept, invalidate the affected approval, review the new content and publish a complete release. Retain redirects for renamed IDs and point saved entries to stable concepts.

## Failure behaviour

| Failure | Expected behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Firebase unavailable or quota exhausted | Public reading/search continues; submission or account feature clearly reports failure |
| Relay rejects an upload | No false success; preserve entered text where feasible and offer direct email |
| Email accepted by relay but not delivered | No claim of inbox delivery; test mailbox routing and follow the manual receipt process |
| Build validation fails | Previous published release stays available |
| Private records are lost | No promised recovery while private backups are deferred |
| Future AI lacks evidence | Say the collection cannot answer; do not invent a source |

These diagrams are authored for Utkal · Odisha with AI assistance. They depict application architecture, not historical evidence or a formal OKF conformance certification.

[Stack and responsibilities](technical-stack.md) · [Growth triggers](growth-roadmap.md)

# Architecture decision register

## Current decisions

These decisions record the user's instructions and the accepted plan in this conversation on 27 September 2026. They do not assert human factual verification or completed implementation. Concept status stays draft until documentation review; public publication approval is separate.

| ID | Decision | Status and rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ADR-001 | Keep the canonical public KB in Git and OKF 0.2 | Agreed. Portable, reviewable source with preserved concept paths and provenance. |
| ADR-002 | Publish visitor-read-only knowledge from that source | Agreed. Visitors can propose changes, not modify the authoritative public dataset directly. |
| ADR-003 | Use Astro + TypeScript, selective React, shared CSS and Pagefind | Agreed stack direction. Use existing content and brand; validate Odia behaviour. |
| ADR-004 | Use GitHub Pages with a user-owned domain | Agreed. Supersedes the Firebase Hosting launch recommendation. Domain registration renews. |
| ADR-005 | Start Firebase on Spark for accounts and private dynamic text | Agreed. Blaze is deferred until a specific capability or quota need justifies it. |
| ADR-006 | Receive photos by email and publish accepted copies through Git | Agreed. A free FormSubmit relay is an untested candidate; direct email is the fallback. Supersedes paid Firebase upload storage and automatic Git export for launch. |
| ADR-007 | Defer AI chat unless an acceptable free alternative is established | Agreed. Keep architecture and evaluations as future work; search is the launch interface. |
| ADR-008 | Defer paid private backups | Agreed. Keep local KB/Git copies; make no private-data recovery guarantee. |
| ADR-009 | Target $0/month in incremental launch services within free limits | Agreed cost direction. Domain renewal, labour and existing coding subscriptions are separate. |
| ADR-010 | Keep evidence review and publication approval distinct from automated checks | Existing project rule retained. No draft data or private fields leak via pages, search or downloads. |

## Inputs to resolve during implementation

- Final repository name, visibility and public-file selection. `ahimanikya` is the intended owner; `odisha-encyclopedia` remains proposed.
- Domain registration, chosen canonical hostname and DNS access.
- Editorial inbox address and form activation; sample attachment delivery must pass before enabling uploads.
- Firebase project, region, authorised domain, maintainer accounts and Security Rules; no billing account is required by the Spark launch design.
- Named editorial responsibilities, publication permissions and reuse licences for content, code and images.
- GA4 property and consent/event configuration, without recording private text.
- Package versions and supported runtime to pin when implementing; no untested model selection.

## Changes deliberately not made

No cloud account, repository remote, paid plan, DNS record, public deployment, email delivery or new monitoring schedule was created by this documentation task. Current architecture replaces earlier proposals; retain the conversation and project log as history, not as parallel active instructions.

instruction_basis: User-agreed launch architecture in the Odisha Tourism conversation, 27 September 2026. Future stages are proposals; no deployment or billing change is implied.
body:
# Technical growth roadmap

## Grow in response to observed needs

Keep the public KB in Git at every stage. Add a service when a concrete need appears, its operating cost is understood and its acceptance checks pass. The measures below are proposed review triggers, not automatic spending authorisation or provider limits. This roadmap has no fixed calendar and creates no scheduled jobs.

| Stage | Trigger | Deliverable and acceptance gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 — Establish the foundation | Current work | Consolidate existing OKF, brand and photo references; preserve IDs; create the intended Git repository and publication allowlist when implementing. No confidential files enter public history. |
| 1 — Launch on free services | One complete pilot is ready | Astro on GitHub Pages, domain/HTTPS, search, sourced photo story, text/email contribution paths and Firebase Spark permissions. Demonstrate one accepted contribution through to public release. |
| 2 — Improve editorial capacity | Suggested trigger: over 20 pending items for two weeks or manual work exceeds two hours/week | Better private review metadata, templates, contributor guidance and delegated roles within Spark where possible. Measure correction turnaround and failed submissions before buying automation. |
| 3 — Reliable uploads and automation | Attachment loss, repeated email limits or measurable review burden | Evaluate Blaze + private Storage/Functions. Obtain an acceptable budget before enabling billing. Test permissions, retry-safe saves, upload limits and reviewed Git export; never auto-publish unreviewed content. |
| 4 — Broader discovery and data | More reviewed districts/languages and repeated cross-topic questions | Expand linked tables, aliases, map-ready places, versioned JSON and optional SQLite downloads. Validate performance on ordinary phones and review Odia language quality. |
| 5 — Ask Utkal | Search leaves recurring questions unanswered and a viable free option or budget exists | Retrieve only approved passages, show source and contributor credit, pass the existing 15 AI acceptance cases plus English/Odia retrieval tests. No free model or gateway is assumed. |
| Recovery track — independent private recovery | Suitable free export method becomes available, or private records become operationally important | Define owners, retention and a protected independent copy; test database, identity and media restoration as appropriate. Paid private backups remain deferred until a revised decision. |

Recovery can be reviewed before any numbered growth stage. Paid AI, backup and Blaze features are not requirements for the agreed first launch.

## Capacity checks and cost decisions

Measure built-site size, Git history size, transfer, image sizes, Firebase quota use, inbox capacity, review backlog and submission failures. Record only aggregate operational metrics; keep private content out of analytics.

Suggested early review points: built output or repository history reaches 500 MB; repeated Firebase use exceeds 70% of a free quota; or any contribution is lost in an intake path. These are our conservative decision thresholds. GitHub Pages currently limits published sites to 1 GB with a soft 100 GB/month bandwidth limit, so review before approaching them. See [Pages limits](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits). Firebase quotas vary by product and reset interval; check the relevant console and [Firestore quotas](https://firebase.google.com/docs/firestore/quotas).

For each upgrade, record the problem, expected monthly use, free allowance, overage rates, privacy/access changes, migration approach, rollback and accountable maintainer. Set appropriate alerts and supported caps; ordinary alerts do not cap all spending. See [billing controls](https://firebase.google.com/docs/projects/billing/avoid-surprise-bills).

The launch service target remains $0/month within free allowances, excluding domain renewal and existing tools. No earlier $10–30/month estimate is an approved launch budget. Re-estimate before enabling paid services; do not treat a free trial as a permanent funding source.

## Migration rules

**Email to managed uploads:** preserve submission IDs, credit and consent scope; transfer pending files privately; test both paths before retiring email. Keep email as a fallback until successful delivery and review have been demonstrated.

**Spark to Blaze:** upgrade only for the selected functionality or capacity. Existing public Git records remain unchanged. Restrict uploads and privileged actions; test rules, receipts, moderation and costs before general access. [Firebase plans](https://firebase.google.com/docs/projects/billing/firebase-pricing-plans) describe the upgrade; [Storage requirements](https://firebase.google.com/docs/storage/faqs-storage-changes-announced-sept-2024) explain billing for uploads.

**Static data to larger datasets:** retain CSV/JSON as source and stable IDs. Build partitioned exports; offer SQL snapshots for research. Move large media only when needed, leaving rights, checksums and canonical references in Git. A graph database or vector store requires demonstrated query or retrieval needs.

**Search to AI:** create an index from the exact approved release; test retrieval separately from answer generation. Cite source passages, qualify historical connections and preserve credit. Do not expose provider credentials in the browser. Free Gemini access has model/usage and data-use conditions; it is not a complete zero-cost chat service by itself. See [Gemini pricing](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing).

**Hosting or backend change:** preserve URLs and redirects, export public and private records separately, retain access rules and test a rollback. Public delivery should remain independent of the private intake backend.

## Community growth alongside the technology

Expand reviewed coverage, the heritage/global-connections atlas, partner directories and supervised student research through the same evidence and publication process. Internships and partnerships remain proposals until real arrangements exist. Broader living-family collection needs a defined consent and access process before intake. Do not infer lineage, ethnicity or religion from a surname or visual similarity.

The weekly data editor already exists. Update its canonical paths and release integration when the repository is connected; do not create a duplicate automation. Preserve its existing authorisation for routine validated updates while enforcing the agreed publication rules. See [weekly data agent](../methods/weekly-data-agent.md).

[Current stack](technical-stack.md) · [Architecture diagrams](architecture.md) · [Decisions](decisions.md)

title: Technical stack for Utkal · Odisha
description: Agreed launch stack, data ownership, photo intake, publishing and operating limits.
instruction_basis: User-agreed launch architecture in the Odisha Tourism conversation, 27 September 2026. Future stages are proposals; no deployment or billing change is implied.
body:
# Technical stack for Utkal · Odisha

## Agreed direction

Use Astro and TypeScript to publish a reading-focused encyclopedia from the existing OKF knowledge collection. Git stores reviewed public knowledge and approved display photos. GitHub Pages delivers the static website through a user-owned domain. Firebase Spark supports identity and private dynamic text data. Photo contributions arrive by email, optionally through a free form relay; editors publish accepted material through Git.

The incremental launch service target is **$0/month within free allowances**, using an existing inbox. Domain registration and renewal are separate. Development time and existing coding subscriptions are excluded. Free allowances are limits, not a permanent guarantee. No remote repository, domain, form service or Firebase project was configured by this documentation update.

| Layer | Launch choice | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Content and version history | GitHub + the existing OKF 0.2 bundle | Markdown concepts, sources, JSON/CSV tables and approved media |
| Website | Astro + TypeScript | Static article, directory, gallery and data pages |
| Interactive UI | React only where useful; shared CSS variables | Forms and reviewer/account screens using the existing brand |
| Public data | Versioned JSON; optional generated SQLite | Visitor-read-only tables and research exports |
| Search | Pagefind | Browser search of published pages |
| Delivery | GitHub Pages + GitHub Actions | Build validation, production artifact, custom domain and HTTPS |
| User identity | Firebase Authentication on Spark | Guest sessions and editor/contributor accounts; avoid SMS |
| Dynamic text data | Firestore Standard on Spark | Proposals, review metadata, preferences and bookmarks |
| Photo intake | Editorial email; FormSubmit candidate | No paid upload storage; activate and test before showing an upload control |
| Publishing | Manual editorial review followed by Git change | No browser-held Git write credential or automatic publication |
| Analytics | GA4 with explicit consent and safe event fields | No raw messages, emails or family details in analytics |
| Local verification | Existing KB validators, Firebase emulators, focused UI tests | Content structure, permission boundaries and real submission handling |

Astro provides content collections; Pagefind indexes static output. These choices serve our content-heavy design without making ordinary readers query a live database. See [Astro](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/content-collections/) and [Pagefind](https://pagefind.app/).

## Data ownership

The canonical collection remains `outputs/odisha-kb/`. Preserve existing concept-path IDs. OKF is the document format; CSV/JSON are application data linked by those concepts. Our schema versions and publication fields are local extensions, not additional OKF requirements. See [the recorded method](../about/research-method.md).

Public tables include places, alternate names, periods, sources, claims, claim-source links, historical relationships, media and public organisations. Include source, period, geography, evidence class and revision where relevant. Keep uncertainty explicit. Generate SQLite from editable text rather than editing two competing databases.

Firestore contains private working data. Bookmarks refer to public concept IDs rather than copied articles. Never commit contact details, consent records, pending photos, account data or credentials to public branches. A public pull request is already public even before merge. Existing research also needs explicit publication selection; lifecycle `stable` is not publication approval.

## Contributions and permissions

Guests may submit text using anonymous Authentication and narrowly scoped Firestore Security Rules. They may create permitted fields, but not self-approve, assign roles or read another person's private record. Rules provide enforcement on Spark; hiding an admin screen is not security. Assign reviewer roles through a controlled maintainer operation. Test invalid writes, repeated requests, expired sessions and cross-user reads with emulators. Client-side checks improve usability but do not provide server-side rate limiting.

Photos use a separate inbox path. A free FormSubmit relay is a candidate, not yet an operational dependency. Its documentation specifies a 10 MB total attachment limit and no recovery of uploaded files from its submission archive. Propose three JPEG/PNG files and 8 MB combined as our smaller UI limit. Keep a direct-email fallback. See [upload documentation](https://formsubmit.co/documentation) and [service description](https://formsubmit.co/).

Collect a caption, approximate date/location if known, public credit, private reply address and explicit permission to publish. Explain that the form forwards details to the editorial inbox. Report successful relay acceptance as “sent for review”, not published or guaranteed inbox delivery. A mailto link only opens an email draft. Activate the recipient and test a real permitted sample before enabling the form.

Editors inspect files, confirm rights and credit, remove unwanted private metadata from display copies, preserve accepted originals locally and add approved copies to Git. Email is the photo queue; any Firestore review record is entered manually at launch. There is no assumed automatic inbox-to-database integration.

## Build and release

A reviewed Git change triggers checks and a static build. Validate IDs, sources, data relationships, media rights and approval tied to the actual content digest. Export only permitted public fields. Emit pages, search data and a release manifest containing Git revision and schema version; version the exported data files together. Failed checks leave the previous release available. Retain a known-good release for public rollback.

Keep untrusted contribution checks isolated from deployment credentials. GitHub Actions uploads only the generated website artifact. Do not copy the entire local KB, private inbox exports or development folders into the public website. At setup, choose a public release repository scope that excludes confidential research from Git history as well as from website output.

GitHub Pages handles static delivery; Firebase SDK requests go separately to Firebase. Add the chosen domain to authorised Authentication settings as applicable. No Firebase Hosting API rewrites are available on GitHub Pages. Public reading and search remain available if Firebase or the mail relay fails.

## Boundaries and launch gates

Deferred: Firebase Blaze, Firebase Storage, Cloud Functions, AI chat and paid private backups. Spark can be upgraded later; it requires no payment method for the supported free features. Storage and server functions need billing-enabled services if added later. See [Firebase plans](https://firebase.google.com/docs/projects/billing/firebase-pricing-plans).

The first complete feature is Bhubaneswar's Painted Streets: credited gallery, searchable story, correction/photo intake, editorial review, Git change and published update. Verify mobile/keyboard use, Odia names and search examples, domain/HTTPS, permission rules, quota failure messages, accurate submit status, source attribution and public rollback. If upload relay testing fails, use email; a working contribution path remains a launch requirement. AI and private backup restoration are not launch gates while deferred.

Keep local KB/Git copies. Private Firebase/inbox recovery is not guaranteed while independent backups are deferred. GA4 remains off until its property and consent behaviour are tested. No raw search queries, form text or lineage details should enter analytics.

title: Bali Jatra: measurable commerce within the celebration
description: Bali Jatra: measurable commerce within the celebration — evidence, scope and reuse.

sources.title: Baliyatra festival sales and footfall report, 23 November 2024

verification_scope: Verified as a reported statement by named officials, not as audited sales.
body:
# Bali Jatra: measurable commerce within the celebration

A 23 November 2024 Times of India report quotes the ORMAS Cuttack chief reporting **₹40 crore in Pallishree Mela sales**, and describes **500 stalls**. It separately quotes the collector on more than ₹250 crore in overall festival business.[^maritime-fair-sales]

## Use with attribution

The ORMAS figure is a subset of the overall fair, not additional sales to add on top. Sales are not profit, household income, tax revenue or net economic impact. The report is not audited accounts.

The page’s title and URL say 2023, while its date and body refer to 2024. The KB records the body’s 2024 attribution and the discrepancy. Obtain the ORMAS closing statement before using this as an unqualified campaign statistic. Do not annualise the event or call it the latest edition’s result.

## Story opportunity

Follow a willing seller from preparing stock to taking orders. Combine the attributed event statistic with that person’s own experience without presenting one stall as representative of every participant.

[Boita Bandana](../culture/boita-bandana.md) · [Research queue](../history/research-agenda.md)

[^maritime-fair-sales]: [Baliyatra festival sales and footfall report, 23 November 2024](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bhubaneswar/baliyatra-festival-2023-concludes-with-record-breaking-business-and-footfall/articleshow/115604020.cms)

title: Historical connections and modern trade: join matrix
description: Historical connections and modern trade: join matrix — evidence, scope and reuse.
body:
# Historical connections and modern trade: join matrix

| Place / region | Historic or cultural link in this KB | Modern measurable link | Join quality |
|---|---|---|---|
| China | Ceramic/coin finds at Manikapatna; Khalkatapatna interpretation | Survey destination share | Strong place-level pairing; no causal or product-level continuity asserted |
| Sri Lanka | Reported coins at Manikapatna | Missing state–country series | Historic evidence available; commercial join incomplete |
| Indonesia / Bali | Festival remembrance and India–Bali archaeological context | Missing Odisha–Indonesia series | Cultural link established; exclusive ancient origin not established |
| Malaysia | Published reconstruction involving Malay Peninsula | Survey destination share | Interpretive historical link; modern national geography differs |
| Vietnam | Odisha-specific historical attribution needs further work | Survey destination share | Modern link established; historical join held |
| Gujarat | Most likely provenance of Manikapatna anchor rock | Bilateral coastal traffic not established | Material link; no present shipment estimate |
| Arabian region | Khalkatapatna research interpretation | No matched region series | Do not substitute one modern country for the whole region |
| Roman world | Direct-route claim questioned by reassessment | Not joined | Excluded from established direct-route claims |

Source-bearing records: [Manikapatna](../history/manikapatna.md), [Khalkatapatna](../history/khalkatapatna.md), [Indonesia](../history/bali-and-indonesia.md), [Malay routes](../history/palur-and-bay-routes.md), [anchor](../history/manikapatna-anchor.md), [Roman review](../history/roman-connection-review.md), and [modern destinations](export-destinations.md).

## What this map can say

“Odisha’s maritime story connects places that matter to commerce today.” It cannot assign a numerical share of another country’s culture to Odisha or calculate growth from ancient trade without ancient quantity data.

The [machine-readable graph](../references/data/maritime-links.jsonld) keeps each relationship attached to its evidence type, period, source and limitation. Missing observations are explicit research gaps.

title: Asia in Odisha’s present export geography
description: Asia in Odisha’s present export geography — evidence, scope and reuse.

sources.title: Odisha Economic Survey 2025–26, section 1.7 and Figure 1.16

verification_scope: Percentages checked against indexed survey paragraph; denominator ambiguity explicitly retained.
body:
# Asia in Odisha’s present export geography

Survey section 1.7.5 lists these FY2024–25 destination shares: **China 21.5%; Malaysia 3.9%; Vietnam 3.5%**. Their reported shares sum to **28.9%**.[^maritime-exports-2026]

## Denominator and scope

The paragraph describes shares of the state’s total export value in a merchandise-focused discussion. Preserve “survey-reported destination shares” until the underlying DEPM/DGCI&S table clarifies goods versus all exports. No country-level rupee estimates are generated here.

These are modern destination observations. They do not show which products each destination bought, which Odisha port carried them, or continuity of a medieval route.

## Historical joins

[China](../history/manikapatna.md) has an archaeological connection in this collection. [Malaysia](../history/palur-and-bay-routes.md) can be paired with a labelled historical route reconstruction. Vietnam has a verified modern observation here, but an Odisha-specific historical link still needs stronger evidence.

[Connection matrix](connection-matrix.md) · [Linked data](../references/data/maritime-links.jsonld)

[^maritime-exports-2026]: [Odisha Economic Survey 2025–26, section 1.7 and Figure 1.16](https://assembly.odisha.gov.in/WriteReadData/News/OES%202026%20WEB%20UPLOAD.pdf)

title: Trade story: supported headlines and captions
description: Trade story: supported headlines and captions — evidence, scope and reuse.
body:
# Trade story: supported headlines and captions

| Headline | Required adjoining caption | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A culture that honours its traders | Editorial interpretation of maritime commemoration | [Boita Bandana](../culture/boita-bandana.md) |
| More than twice the cargo. One decade. | Paradip; FY2015–16 to FY2025–26; cargo throughput in million tonnes | [Port comparison](paradip-throughput.md) |
| Goods exports, 81% higher over five years | Odisha; FY2019–20 to FY2024–25; nominal rupee value; endpoint comparison | [Merchandise record](merchandise-exports.md) |
| China. Malaysia. Vietnam. Odisha is connected. | Contemporary survey destination observations; not a claim of uninterrupted historical routes | [Destination shares](export-destinations.md) |
| A stone with a journey to tell | Researchers identify Gujarat as the most likely rock source of the Manikapatna anchor | [Archaeometric finding](../history/manikapatna-anchor.md) |

## Hold or rewrite

“Odisha created Southeast Asian civilisation” has no defensible basis in this collection. “Continuous world trade for 2,000 years” is not established by dated finds. “Paradip’s cargo is all Odisha exports” misstates coverage. “Bali Jatra generated ₹250 crore of GDP” confuses reported transactions with value added. “Every Odia is an entrepreneur” is an unsupported generalisation.

Use “participated in exchange,” “commemorates maritime traders,” and “building the next chapter” where those match the evidence. Keep a claim’s scope visible in the main caption rather than relying on an unreadable footnote to repair a misleading headline.

title: Odisha merchandise exports: five-year scale change
description: Odisha merchandise exports: five-year scale change — evidence, scope and reuse.

sources.title: Odisha Economic Survey 2025–26, section 1.7 and Figure 1.16

verification_scope: Indexed official section 1.7.2; arithmetic recomputed.
body:
# Odisha merchandise exports: five-year scale change

The survey reports **₹47,240 crore in FY2019–20** and **₹85,540 crore in FY2024–25**. These endpoints imply **81.1% nominal growth**, or **12.61% CAGR**.[^maritime-exports-2026]

## Reuse

Use “81% higher over five years” with the years and current-price basis visible. This endpoint comparison does not establish growth every year, an inflation-adjusted increase or a record peak.

## Measure boundaries

Merchandise means goods. Do not substitute the survey’s larger goods-plus-services figure or port tonnage. A country-share table also needs its own denominator; do not infer a rupee amount for a destination until that basis is reconciled.

[Stored metrics and formula](../references/data/maritime-metrics.json) · [Destination shares](export-destinations.md)

[^maritime-exports-2026]: [Odisha Economic Survey 2025–26, section 1.7 and Figure 1.16](https://assembly.odisha.gov.in/WriteReadData/News/OES%202026%20WEB%20UPLOAD.pdf)

# Paradip: the institutional bridge between memory and commerce

Paradip Port Authority organised Boita Bandana on 27 November 2023. The President attended and inaugurated a multimodal logistics park; other facilities in the release were at foundation-stone stage.[^maritime-paradip-ritual]

## Why this connection is strong

The same named institution appears in a cultural event record and in modern cargo statistics. That is a documented link, not an assumed economic effect of a festival.

Use it to move a film from miniature boats to the port’s contemporary work. Attribute any filmed workers and secure access. The event proves institutional participation in remembrance; it does not prove uninterrupted organisational descent from ancient merchants.

[Cargo performance](paradip-throughput.md) · [Boita Bandana](../culture/boita-bandana.md)

[^maritime-paradip-ritual]: [President of India graces Boita Bandana ceremony at Paradip](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1980175)

title: Paradip: cargo has more than doubled over a decade
description: Paradip: cargo has more than doubled over a decade — evidence, scope and reuse.

sources.title: Paradip port registers historic high cargo handling in FY 25–26

verification_scope: Source endpoints rechecked; arithmetic reproducible.
body:
# Paradip: cargo has more than doubled over a decade

Cargo handled rose from **76.39 million tonnes in FY2015–16** to **156.45 million tonnes in FY2025–26**: **104.8% growth**, calculated from the reported endpoints.[^maritime-paradip-2016][^maritime-paradip-2026]

The latest port release identifies **65.81 million tonnes**, or **42.06%**, as coastal cargo.[^maritime-paradip-2026]

## Interpretation

This is all-cargo throughput, not Odisha-origin exports or international trade alone. It measures a port’s activity, including cargo serving a wider hinterland. Capacity is a different variable.

## Reuse

Headline: “More than twice the cargo. One decade.” Place the port name, financial years and unit immediately below it. The comparison is not an all-India ranking.

[Calculation data](../references/data/maritime-metrics.json) · [Institutional bridge](paradip-bridge.md)

[^maritime-paradip-2016]: [Increasing efficiency of Major Ports](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1513070)
[^maritime-paradip-2026]: [Paradip port registers historic high cargo handling in FY 25–26](https://paradipport.gov.in/all_news/paradip-port-registers-historic-high-cargo-handling-in-fy-25-26-best-ever-in-its-history/)

title: Growing the Odisha discovery indexes
description: Growing the Odisha discovery indexes — visitor index research.
body:
# Growing the Odisha discovery indexes

Build positive impressions through specific things a reader can discover, experience, buy or share. Start with useful linked collections; introduce comparison scores only when their method and coverage justify them.

| Sequence | Index | Reader benefit | Evidence to collect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Now | Food + heritage + nearby services | Turn curiosity into a possible visit | Place links, named providers, access, routes, services |
| Next | Woven & made | Discover skills and buy from credited makers | Maker identity, technique, workshop access, buying route |
| Next | Nature & weekends | Find a reason to return | Seasonal access, permits, transport, hosts |
| Then | Festivals & living culture | Plan around shared experiences | Organiser-confirmed dates, participation rules, local voices |
| Then | Family & accessible visits | Match a trip to actual needs | Feature-level access checks, toilets, rest areas, route conditions |
| Later | Active Odisha | Discover sports, movement and wellness experiences | Current venues, instructors, trails and practical access |
| Later | Enterprise & growth | Connect pride with trade possibilities | Comparable multi-year outcomes, realised facilities, credited businesses |

## Geographic expansion

Deepen the five seed areas, then extend to Koraput, southern Odisha, western Odisha and additional northern/coastal destinations. Use the existing place, food and handloom records as research starting points. Do not interpret the first collection’s coastal/city concentration as a ranking of regions.

## Useful measures

Track complete visitor pages, destinations with linked food providers, credited makers, operational details checked within their review window and reader actions such as saved trips or enquiries. These measure this project’s coverage and response. They do not establish statewide tourism quality, cleanliness, economic impact or happiness.

## Public experience

**Explore → Taste → Plan your visit → Meet the makers → Discover more.**

Lead with an inviting detail and a credited image. Let the reader expand sources and practical information. Show a specific next action, such as checking the official museum page or contacting a featured maker, once that route is established.


## Learning from the official tourism portal · 30 September 2026

The [reference study](../about/odisha-tourism-study.md) examines nine sampled pages and proposes place/interest/planning entrances, consistent destination modules and explicit itinerary evidence. The local visitor index now offers those reading paths. The [trip-content template](../methods/trip-planning-content.md) guides research; interactive filters, map planning, route optimisation and booking remain proposals, not additions to the launch requirements. PRD v0.2.0 and its preserved snapshots are unchanged.

# Puri and craft places: a sourced journey outline

**Research outline, checked 1 October 2026.** Connect appliqué in Pipili and Pattachitra in Raghurajpur with Puri's heritage. The order below has a published operator basis; Utkal has not checked it on the ground or established a trip duration, budget or bookable workshop.

## Source and sequence

[Om Leisure Holidays' itinerary on Odisha Tourism](https://apps.odishatourism.gov.in/tour/wonders-of-odisha-tourist-destinations), Day 02, describes driving from Bhubaneswar through Dhauli, Pipili and Raghurajpur to Puri. This is a commercial itinerary hosted on a government portal. The portal's presence does not independently validate service delivery or access rules.

**Bhubaneswar → Dhauli → Pipili → Raghurajpur → Puri.** Dhauli is retained as a source-named intermediate stop, with its own access profile still to research. This is a one-way outline; the starting pickup and final drop-off addresses are unknown.

| Travel connection | What is established | What remains unknown |
|---|---|---|
| Bhubaneswar → Pipili, via Dhauli | Operator's published road sequence | Pickup, Dhauli access, route geometry, distance and travel time |
| Pipili → Raghurajpur | Consecutive stops in the same published drive | Exact entrances, road conditions, distance and travel time |
| Raghurajpur → Puri | Next destination in the published drive | Drop-off, parking, distance and travel time |

These legs are our decomposition of one published sequence, not separately measured journeys. No current bus route, fare, departure or last-mile connection has been verified. The operator's day label and displayed time window are not Utkal's feasibility estimate.

[Heritage Tours' different package](https://www.heritagetoursorissa.com/golden-triangle-odisha/) places Pipili on its Konark drive and Raghurajpur after a Puri stay. It offers a separate route example, not confirmation of the combined sequence above. No advertised price is adopted.

## Stops and conditions

- [Bhubaneswar](../cities/bhubaneswar.md): start locality; pickup unknown.
- [Pipili appliqué](../culture/pipili-applique.md): craft context; shop, demonstration, host consent and appointment unknown.
- [Raghurajpur and Pattachitra](../culture/raghurajpur-pattachitra.md): craft context; individual workshop access and host consent unknown.
- [Puri](../places/puri.md): destination locality. [Jagannath Temple](../places/jagannath-temple-puri.md) is a conditional visit, not the road leg's precise endpoint. Official tourism hours conflict, and current temple-authority entry arrangements remain unverified. Operator access claims do not resolve this.

## Before a recommendation

Identify consenting hosts, source pickup/drop-off and every travel leg, confirm visitor-specific temple access, allow for meals and breaks, and check toilets, water, mobility needs and seasonal changes. Named food/stay leads are available, but there is no confirmed meal, room or supplier assignment for this outline. Nimapada remains outside this route; its area association alone does not establish a detour.

A knowledgeable local reviewer and a second editor have not reviewed the assembled route. No interviews, site visits, contact requests, media permissions or bookings took place. Keep total duration, budget, leg distances and times blank until supported. Recheck unavailable official transport evidence on or after 8 October 2026; local participation requires a later authorised review workflow.

[Structured route evidence](../references/data/puri-journey-research.json) preserves each connection and its missing fields.

[Puri craft area](areas/puri-crafts.md) — Connect the route outline with place-access evidence; geographic sequence does not resolve entry permissions or opening conflicts.

[Guide and provider research](puri-providers.md) — Use provider listings to identify verification leads; listing does not establish a booking or a consenting craft host.

# Bhāsvatī

A practical astronomical handbook attributed to Śatānanda, dated to 1099 CE in the modern study. Panda describes eight chapters and 128 verses, including calendar, planetary-position and eclipse calculations and a centesimal computational method. These counts describe a text, not a statewide scientific-output measure.

The English-language historical study is available at [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.03661); it is not a complete English translation of the handbook. Selected catalogue witnesses are now recorded below; original folio inspection, edition identity and independent specialist review remain open. Do not claim invention of the decimal system, exact modern accuracy or measured international impact.

[Contributor](../people/satananda.md).

## Catalogue witnesses · 1 October 2026

[Manuscript evidence](../history/scientific-manuscripts.md) now links this existing work to four selected IGNCA catalogue descriptions in Pune, Guwahati and Varanasi. # Studying multiple chronic conditions in Odisha primary care

[Sanghamitra Pati’s profile](../people/sanghamitra-pati.md) connects the paper to her Bhubaneswar research work.

# Spark of Light: Short Stories by Women Writers of Odisha

**A ready reading route into Odisha’s literature:** this English anthology was published by Athabasca University Press in December 2016, edited by Valerie Henitiuk and Supriya Kar. Its contents list **26 named women authors**, spanning early and later Odia writing. This is the anthology’s coverage, not a statewide count or a popularity ranking.

Paperback ISBN 9781771991674; PDF ISBN 9781771991681; EPUB ISBN 9781771991698. DOI: 10.15215/aupress/9781771991674.01. Editors, story authors and translators have separate roles. Only five selected stories and their author links are indexed individually here so far.

[Publisher catalogue and free PDF](https://www.aupress.ca/books/120262-spark-of-light/). The publisher states CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; cover-photo rights are separately credited in the book. Availability of a download is not permission for unrestricted marketing reuse.

**Editorial opportunity:** introduce readers to a story, its writer and translator, then invite them to read the publisher’s edition. Poverty, inequality and women’s constraints remain part of the literary discussion; cultural promotion should not erase the authors’ subjects.

[The Mendicant](the-mendicant.md) — This story is a component of the anthology; do not count the container and its contents as independent books.

[The Vigil](the-vigil.md) — This story is a component of the anthology; do not count the container and its contents as independent books.

Springer’s subtitle places the joint CMMR/FRSM meeting in Bhubaneswar, 9–12 March **2011**; the book editions appeared in **2012**.

Print ISBN **978-3-642-31979-2**, dated 1 July 2012; ebook ISBN **978-3-642-31980-8**, dated 2 July 2012. DOI: [10.1007/978-3-642-31980-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-31980-8). LNCS volume **7172**.

Editing this collection does not make each editor the author of every contribution. The [Odia speech chapter](odia-speech-wiener-filter-2012.md) has its own credited authors. Metadata and contents were inspected; full book and reuse rights were not reviewed.

# Yajnaseni: The Story of Draupadi

Translator Pradip Bhattacharya’s bibliography confirms his English translation of Pratibha Ray’s novel, **Rupa, 1995**, ISBN **9788171673230**. Keep this English edition distinct from the original Odia edition and later impressions.

Metadata and source links establish a reading or research route. Reproduction rights, live stock and complete work review are not established.

[Creator profile](../people/pratibha-ray.md) — Connect this work with its credited creator; recognition of a person is distinct from sales or impact of this work.

## Original-language edition evidence · 1 October 2026

The [Library of Congress reading list](https://www.loc.gov/acq/overseas-offices/delhi/salrp/pratibharay.html) names a first edition: Kataka, Nalanda, **1984**, LCCN **87901017**. The linked catalogue-record fetch failed, and the same page’s biography gives 1985. A [publisher description](https://www.blackeaglebooks.org/product/jagyaseni/) also contains both years.

We therefore record the specific 1984 edition listing while leaving the unqualified original-publication year unresolved. The publisher’s claim of 110 editions does not establish print runs, sales or readership. The existing 1995 English translation record remains separate.
